News.title: Missing girl, 17, feared to be in woods with wanted man, 37, & two dogs as cops launch huge search operation
News.content:
FIND RACHEL Missing girl, 17, feared to be in woods with wanted man, 37, & two dogs as cops launch huge search operation

A TEENAGE girl who disappeared three days ago is reportedly living with a man in the woods.

The desperate hunt for missing Rachel, 17, has led cops to believe that she is living in woods in Doncaster with a man called Craig Clarkson, 39.



Rachel, from the Suffolk area, was first reported missing on July 23 with police thinking she had travelled to the Doncaster area.

After further enquiries, South Yorkshire Police released CCTV images of Rachel and Craig leaving a shop together in Carcroft.



As cops continue to frantically search for the teen, Craig has now become a wanted man in connection with Rachel’s disappearance.

It’s believed he could be carrying a large rucksack and two dogs.



Specialist search teams, uniformed officers, and detectives are involved in the search and are extremely concerned for her welfare.

Rachel is described as a slim white woman with light coloured hair and a distinctive tattoo on her right hand.



Craig is described as a slim white man and is also known to frequent the Clay Ponds area of Askern.

Detective Inspector Adam Watkinson said: “I want to start by making it very clear that Rachel is not in any sort of trouble with the police.

“We have become extremely concerned for her welfare and are working as hard as possible to find her and check that she is safe.

“Our enquiries have led us to suspect that Craig Clarkson has been travelling with Rachel since her disappearance from Suffolk, and we are now treating him as a wanted person in connection with this investigation.

“If anyone sees him, please call 999 immediately. It is essential that we speak to Clarkson and make sure Rachel is safe as soon as possible.”



A spokesperson for the force said: “Craig Clarkson, aged 39, and Rachel were last seen outside the Rose store in the Carcroft area of Doncaster on the morning of 23 July.

“Officers believe it is possible that Craig and Rachel are in woodland near Long Lands Lane, and we’re asking anyone who frequents the area known as Brodsworth Woodland to keep an eye out.

“Our enquiries have led us to believe that she could be with a man whom we are now treating as wanted in connection with her disappearance.

“If you see Clarkson and Rachel, or something that suggests they may have been in the area recently, please report it straight away.”

News.title: Influencer Sara Gilson’s harrowing final moments on child’s 911 call after outing ‘pedophile hubby caught abusing girl’
News.content:
INFLUENCER Sara Gilson’s harrowing final moments before she was killed in her home have been captured on a 911 call made by one of her children.

The 43-year-old mom of two was found dead alongside her soon-to-be ex-husband Jeremiah “Shawn” Duffey at her home in Collinsville, Oklahoma, on Thursday.



Both suffered gunshot wounds in what investigators say was a murder-suicide enacted by Duffey who Gilson had publicly accused of being a pedophile just weeks before her death.

Investigators say he entered the home, ignoring a protective order that ordered him to stay away from Gilson, opened fire at her, and then turned the gun on himself.



Now, a 911 call obtained by PEOPLE has revealed further harrowing details about the incident, including that at least some of what took place was witnessed by at least one of the children in the home.

The call was made by a child who lived at the property at around 11:15pm in which Gilson could be heard “screaming and crying.”

read more on news FIND HER Therapist, 44, vanishes from idyllic Caribbean island as husband issues plea



“I could hear a female in the background screaming and crying. Some sort of loud bang in the background,” the dispatcher is heard telling first responders en-route to the home.

They arrived at 11:18pm where they found the bodies of the estranged couple.

On July 11, less than two weeks before her death, Gilson posted a TikTok video following a popular trend re-creating a sit-down interview for a Netflix documentary.

“Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile,” she wrote, adding “I wish I was joking.”



The clip has been viewed by over five million people.

Court documents seen by PEOPLE show that a month earlier, on June 10, a woman filed a protective order against Duffey, a basketball coach, claiming that her 15-year-old daughter who was on the team had been abused by him.

She alleged that the 48-year-old had been seen kissing and fondling her daughter by another coach and that her daughter subsequently told her that it was not the first time he was inappropriate with her, The Oklahoman reported.

Duffey is also accused of sending messages to the child inviting her to his hotel room while on a tournament trip and trying to bribe her with cash “to keep her quiet.”



The team coach who witnessed the alleged assault while Duffey was alone with the minor “immediately intervened and reported it to the juvenile’s parents,” Owasso Police said.

In the meantime, Duffey fled the scene and cops called Gilson to inform her of the incident and on how to file protection orders against him, which she did, along with a divorce.

In those emergency protection documents, seen by The Oklahoman, she claimed he had a gun, was threatening to commit suicide and “went on the run.”

She appeared in court a month ago to stand up her claims for protection and Duffey was ordered to leave the home and stay at least 100 yards away from her.



A GoFundMe page has been established by Gilson’s friends in an effort to raise money to support her two children.

“Last night, our beautiful friend, Sara, was tragically taken from us in an unimaginable act of violence,” the friends wrote.

“Her sudden and heartbreaking loss has left an entire community grieving, but the greatest loss is felt by her two precious children, who must now face life without their loving mother.

“Sara was an incredible mom. Her children were the center of her world, and everything she did was for them.

“She loved them fiercely, worked hard to provide for them, and dreamed of giving them the best life possible.”



If you are experiencing domestic violence, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline for free at 1-800-799-7233 or go to thehotline.org.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline at 800-422-4453 or live chat at childhelphotline.org.

If a child or other person is in immediate danger, contact 911 immediately.

News.title: Therapist Elizabeth Waddell, 44, vanishes while on idyllic Caribbean island vacation as husband issues desperate plea
News.content:
PARADISE MYSTERY Therapist Elizabeth Waddell, 44, vanishes while on idyllic Caribbean island vacation as husband issues desperate plea

A PHYSICAL therapist has vanished while vacationing on an idyllic Caribbean island as her husband issues a desperate plea for her safe return.

Elizabeth “Liz” Waddell, 44, from North Carolina, was last seen on July 22 at Grand Anse Beach in St. George’s, Grenada, where she was holidaying without her husband.



Waddell was staying at the dreamy beach resort where she was last seen at 8pm local time.

Her husband, Cailen Waddell, with whom she shares an adopted daughter, has demanded “nothing less than her safe return.”



He flew to the island on Friday to help join the desperate search.

Sharing the missing persons alert on Facebook, he said: “My wife Liz is missing in Grenada.



“If any of you have connections to the island – can you please share the following with your contacts there?”

“I expect nothing less than Liz’s safe return – so please send your love, light, thoughts, and prayers our way,” he added.

The Royal Grenada Police Force described Waddell as 5-foot-5, with a medium build and short blonde hair in the news release.

“We specially appeal to fishermen, boat operators, and residents along the southern coastline to report any sightings or relevant information that may assist in locating Ms. Waddell,” they wrote.



Family friend Amanda Romano-Harmon described Waddell as a wonderful person, while raising fears that something may have happened to her while she had gone for a swim.

“She’s an amazing person, and we want to bring her home,” Romano-Harmon told ABC affiliate WTVD.

“It seems that she went down to the pier and left her towel on the pier and went for a swim.”

Romano-Harmon and her husband go way back with the Waddells, the outlet reported. Her husband Shawn was Cailen’s college roommate.



“Our daughter is 16, and she refers to them as her aunt and uncle, because we’re just that close,” Romano-Harmon told the outlet.

Waddell built Art of Movement Physical Therapy from the ground up, bringing a decade in physical therapy and more than 20 years in fitness and dance to the practice, according to her website.

Her bio said: When not helping people feel awesome, Liz stays active with olympic weightlifting, pole dancing, CrossFit, hiking, traveling, and taking walks with her husband, Cailen, to patronize the downtown Cary small business scene.”

Anyone with information about Waddell’s whereabouts is asked to contact the South Saint George Police Station or the Criminal Investigation Department.

News.title: Heavily pregnant woman, 21, stabbed to death before killer rips baby from womb as cops desperately search for newborn
News.content:
A MUM-TO-BE was kidnapped, stabbed to death and had her baby ripped from her womb, days after revealing that she was going to have a girl.

María Camila Potosí, who was eight months pregnant, disappeared after leaving for a routine antenatal check on July 16.



The 21-year-old was found on Monday, wrapped in sheets and underneath a pile of blankets, four miles away from her home in Cali, Colombia.

When police lifted the pile, they saw that she had been stabbed multiple times – and that her unborn child had been cut from her womb and was missing.



The victim’s hands and feet were tied, and signs of torture were visible on her body.

CCTV footage from the afternoon of María’s disappearance captured her final known movements.

She was seen climbing onto the back of a motorcycle ridden by a woman she met two months earlier through a local support scheme for pregnant women.

That rider has reportedly given changing accounts to investigators and remains a central focus of the inquiry.

Police are still searching for the missing child.

María’s mother, Alba Gomez, has urged the killers to return her granddaughter, who she has named Alahia, Colombian news outlet RCN Noticias reported.



“The only thing I ask with this appeal and with the hopeful faith I hold that my baby is alive – is for her to be found,” she said.

“I ask that the people who have her search their hearts and return her to me.”

Earlier in the day of her kidnapping, her daughter had helped care for a sick relative at her sister-in-law’s home in Meléndez before heading to her appointment.



She then sent a quick message to her mother about a last-minute medical errand. Her husband raised the alarm when she failed to return home.

Prior to her disappearance, María posted images of a joyous gender-reveal gathering online.

Surrounded by gifts and balloons, she is seen smiling while standing next to her husband. She was due to give birth in just a few weeks.

María made the proud moment her WhatsApp profile picture.

Relatives remembered her as kind, innocent and overly trusting, a young woman whose greatest dream was simply to become a mother and build a family home.



The case is being investigated as a possible feminicide, but no arrests have been made yet.

Cali human rights ombudsman Gerardo Mendoza demanded a “swift, exhaustive investigation with a gender focus”.

He added that the “extreme gravity” of the crime “cannot go unpunished”.

Meanwhile, senator-elect Jennifer Pedraza said about the case: “They kidnapped, tortured and murdered a 21-year-old pregnant woman.

“In this country, nothing happens. We demand justice.”



Former presidential candidate Sondra Macollins said: “What impotence this causes. We trust that the Public Prosecutor’s Office and police will deliver rigorous answers.”

News.title: Our son was stabbed to death by a released prisoner – will Burnham keep his promise so this can never happen again?
News.content:
THE family of a dad killed by a released prisoner have called on the PM to fulfil his promise to them and reform the “broken” justice system.

Ten years ago, Michael Hoolickin, 27, was murdered by “feral and animalistic” Timothy Deakin, who should never have been on the streets.



Michael, who leaves behind a son, Ellis, was on a night out when he saw the thug hitting his own sister and bravely stepped in to defend her, telling him “you shouldn’t hit a woman.”

Deakin – who was on probation after being jailed for biting a man’s ear off – then stabbed Michael five times in the chest and stomach outside the Manchester pub in 2016.



The 23-year-old had been let out on licence eight months earlier after serving half of a four-and-a-half year sentence.

He was deemed “high risk” but freed under supervision – despite being a risk to life, specifically to men of a similar age.

The lag was supposed to obey stringent conditions, but was not recalled despite being arrested for driving offences and drug possession.

Have you been affected by the early release of prisoners? Email emily.davies@thesun.co.uk

An inquest into Michael’s death found several missed opportunities by the probation service that contributed to his murder.

Michael’s dad Garry slammed the “shameful” probation system, telling The Sun nothing has changed since his son’s death – and that Andy Burnham promised to back his family in their fight for justice last year.



It comes as a controversial sentencing shake-up means rapists, sex offenders and killers could be released from jail early, from September.

The new PM has paused the “deplorable” scheme and ordered an urgent review after a furious backlash from victims’ families.

The plan was meant to tackle overcrowding in prisons, but FOI data shows 622 alleged murders were committed by a lag on probation between 2014 and 2020 – one every three days.



Garry told The Sun: “It’s just a huge pocket of families being denied true justice here, and it’s just shameful. It really is shameful.

“This kid should never have been on the street – and it was all hidden from us.

“He shouldn’t have been out. He should have been recalled 51 times. And the probation services didn’t do it and they’ve not been held accountable.

“If they had, my son might still be alive. It’s gotten worse, to be honest, we know it’s gotten worse.”

Deakin was described as “feral and lawless” by officials, an inquest heard.



Probation case manager Natalia Atkinson wanted him to be recalled, but shockingly senior probation officer Catherine Entwistle told the inquest she “had not read the emails” sent to her about Deakin.

Deakin was jailed for life with a minimum of 27 years. But in another failure, Garry says he has received an email informing him the killer was moved to a lower security Category C prison – four years ago.

Retired footballer Garry, 67, is one of several families who have banded together to form an organisation called VOICE and call for an inquiry into the probation system.

They met with Burnham several times to discuss the scandal before he was Prime Minister, and he came to show his support when VOICE was launched last year.

Garry added: “The mess within the probation seems to be immune to any sort of legislation, any statutory inquiries. They’re not covered by any laws, any codes.



“Hopefully Andy will keep to his word now and do major changes at least to this failed probation service.”

Michael’s mum Lesley said: “Every day, I don’t like listening to the news because when I hear that people have been stabbed to death, well it just breaks my heart.

“Because I know exactly what it’s all about and I know how the families are feeling and it’s horrific.”



Burnham said at the launch of VOICE: “I first met the Hoolickins a few years ago. I honestly was shocked to hear about the failures that had led to Michael’s death, and the lack of openness, accountability to the family, failure to get to the truth about what happened.

“For me, I particularly remember the reforms to the probation service around the time that Michael died.

“There were so many warnings in Parliament about what was being done and how it might throw things into chaos. They were all ignored.

“The probation service did go into chaos with devastating consequences for the family.”

In 2013, the heavily criticised Transforming Rehabilitation reforms changed how probation was organised and delivered, spitting up the management of high-risk offenders and low to medium-risk criminals.



Burnham said: “I’ve always supported their campaign. I said to Garry, Lesley, and the family that I would back them all the way.

“It’s not just the Hoolickins. There’s so many families all in the same boat, all been treated the same way, with a complete lack of respect, lack of openness, it’s just not right.

“Victims should be at the heart of the system, but they’re being treated as an oversight, they’re just kind of missed or pushed to the side.

“We need answers. We need a review of the probation service. How was this allowed to happen? I strongly support the calls VOICE is making. They have my support all the way. We need justice.”

VOICE believes there are other families out there who have no idea their loved one was killed by a criminal on probation.



Garry said it has taken ten years for the Serious Further Offence (SFO) report to be released to the family.

A SFO is a specific violent and/or sexual offence committed by people who are under probation supervision or have very recently been under probation supervision at the time of the offence.

Families of victims are entitled to see these documents, but a report found many are given it “months or even years” after a conviction.

Data shows that criminals on probation have committed more than 750 murders and sex attacks in the past five years.

More than 40 per cent of SFOs are committed by people who were mistakenly classified as “medium risk” right before the crime happened, a probation report found.



In 2023-2024 there were 56 offenders convicted of murder while under probation supervision.

The report found a “consistent and concerning trend” with probation-led reviews as public protection issues are being driven by underlying system failings, including massive backlogs and understaffing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Families also reported a lack of support, engagement and “limited compassion”.

The Ministry of Justice has been approached for comment.

News.title: Postmen defend Royal Mail worker who kicked blind Shih Tzu before she died as pet owners ‘laugh off attacks on posties’
News.content:
POSTMEN have come to the defence of a Royal Mail worker who kicked a blind Shih Tzu before she died.

The unidentified parcel delivery man was caught on camera booting the pooch, Ethel, outside the family home in Aylesbury, Bucks.



Ethel was rushed to the vets but her injuries proved fatal and she sadly passed away.

Now, following a wave of backlash online, postal workers have come out in defence of the man’s attack.



“I kicked a terrier that bit my leg to get it off me, and I would do it again,” one postman told The Telegraph.

“I would say about 10 of us in my office have been bitten.

“It’s very common, and it’s always the dogs that have ‘never done that before’.”

Another added: “I felt for that dog and the owner but I also felt for the postie.



“If you have been bitten, or been threatened with being bitten, it makes you scared.

“They come snapping at your ankles and it’s frightening.”

Around 2,019 dog attacks were reported last year on postal workers, according to Royal Mail.

Of those, 61 had caused significant injuries to employees.

It is reported that half of these attacks happened at the front door, with a quarter occurring in a garden, drive, or yard.



After being left with a bleeding cut by a dog, a postman said that pet owners “laugh it off”.

He also claimed that it was deemed “socially acceptable” for a dog to attack delivery workers.

The postie alleged that that many pet owners were “thoughtless” after attacks.

The driver that kicked the 11-year-old Shih Tzu has reportedly been suspended by Royal Mail.

Royal Mail have also promised to pay Ethel’s family’s vet bills and launched an investigation into the incident.



The incident was caught on Eve Lewis’s Ring Doorbell, showing the man, dressed in an England football shirt hoofing Ethel.

The small pooch flew through the air and rolled along the ground.

She told The Sun that the incident was particularly shocking as her dog was partially blind and only had one tooth, and therefore posed no threat to the worker.

The 40-year-old took Ethel to the vets, who sadly could not save her.

They concluded that she died from organ failure caused by blunt force trauma.



A Royal Mail spokeswoman told The Sun: “Dog-related incidents can present a serious risk to postal workers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We take our responsibility to protect colleagues very seriously, providing practical guidance and support and taking immediate action where a dog presents a risk to their safety or prevents deliveries from being made safely.

“Dog owners have an important role to play by keeping pets secure and away from the door when deliveries are being made.”

News.title: How students discovered four of their housemates had been stabbed to death at home in chilling text sent by uni
News.content:
KAYLEE Goncalves and Madison Mogen were inseparable. Best friends since childhood, they did everything together – even attending the same university in Idaho.

When they shared an apartment off campus with three other girls – Bethany Funke, Dylan Mortensen and Xana Kernodle – they felt like soul mates.



Xana’s likeable boyfriend and fellow student, Ethan Chapin, was also there for much of the time and they would all socialise together.

It was known as a fun, party house, where people would come and go, when not studying. But their dreams for the future were brutally ended for four of them in the early hours of the morning of 13 November 2022 when an intruder entered and savagely butchered them before making his escape.



The incident shocked the community, the country and the world as word spread about this night of horror.

Four years on, the harrowing Sky documentary, The Idaho Murders, features extensive police bodycam footage at the scene of the crime, new insights and the lasting impact on the wider community in this quiet college town of Moscow in Idaho.



“They’ve demolished the house in King Road, where it happened,” says former student at the University of Idaho, Taylor Dolezal.

“The owner of the house gave it to the university and the university decided, ‘We are tearing it down. We’re just going to demolish it. It really helped with the closure of this case.

“Moscow will always be changed because of this. I think, ultimately, the spirit of the university, the fact that it is a college town, means it will bounce back. But there will always be kind of a heaviness surrounding the place, unfortunately.”

On the day before the murders, the local football team had a match. As usual on such Saturdays, there was drinking and socialising by excited fans, before and after the game.

An ominous fog swept in early evening and the temperature dropped. After the football had ended, the five friends made plans to go out.



Bethany and Dylan went home to 1122 King Road earlier than the others and went to bed. Kaylee and Madison returned together in the early hours, as did Xana and Ethan.

The last one to bed was Xana, who had ordered a food delivery that arrived around 4am.

Tragically, there was another arrival – a tall, slim man dressed in black with a balaclava that just showed his eyes and “bushy eyebrows” as Dylan recalled.

A tired Dylan was awoken several times during the night – first by Kaylee’s dog, whining, then somebody crying and later thumping and a female saying “I think someone’s here.”

Then she heard a male voice say, “It’s okay. I’m going to help you.”



Thinking that it was one of the other girl’s boyfriends staying over, she went back to bed until she was awoken by more moving around. When she opened her door to look out, she was terrified to see a man in black walking towards her.

She shut her door, frozen in fear, locked it and heard him leave out of the glass, sliding door, in the kitchen.

Calling her roommates, she got no answer but met up with Bethany downstairs.



After finding Xana lying on the floor, the girls made a panicky emergency call, saying: “Something’s happened in our house and we don’t know what. One of the roommates is passed out. She was drunk last night and she’s not waking up. And they saw some man in the house last night.”

Police arrived and saw blood soaking into the carpets and mattresses and splattered on the walls.

Anthony Dahlinger, Chief of Police, Moscow Police Department, recalls, “It was an horrific scene. Something I will never forget.”

Kaylee and Madison had been repeatedly stabbed to death as they slept in the same bed together. Ethan was in bed, with his jugular slit.

Xana had begun to eat her food when she had been disturbed by the intruder. She had been stabbed over 50 times, with lots of defensive wounds, indicating that there had been a struggle.



“They were just young college kids, going to school to get an education and go out and enjoy their lives,” says Anthony.

“There was nothing obvious as to why someone would want to harm them.”

While survivors, Bethany and Dylan sat outside the house with some friends, police searched the house. At this stage, they did not know that their housemates were dead.

It was only when their university sent a text alert to all students that police were on site investigating a quadruple homicide that they knew.



The documentary shows them at the moment of receiving the text, crying in horror and disbelief.

With the killer still on the loose and the police with no idea who it was, fear rapidly spread throughout the town. Would the attacker strike again?

“We all felt incredibly heartbroken and scared and we wanted to make some sense of how something like this could happen,” says Taylor Dolezal.

“It was inconceivable. We were terrified that there were going to be more. That it wouldn’t stop at the four.”



Police believed the intruder had entered through the sliding glass door in the kitchen. No viable fingerprints on it were found but the killer had left behind something that proved to be crucial – a tan-coloured knife sheath on Madison’s bed.

Desperate to find the murderer as quick as possible, fearing he might strike again, Moscow Police got the FBI and state police involved.

They were jubilant when the sheath was found to have single male DNA on it. Another vital discovery was CCTV footage of a car, identified as a white Hyundai Elantra, making multiple passes around the house for almost an hour on the day of the murders.

Eventually it parked, off camera and then around 4.20am, the car took off

at speed, out of the neighbourhood and almost hit a rubbish bin on the side of the road.

There was no match of the DNA on the databases but experts in DNA genealogy were able to create a genome, identifying that it had above 80 per cent of Italian lineage.



They began to build a family tree until they found one couple whose child

was likely to be the person with the DNA found on the sheath. That couple only had one child – a son, named Bryan Kohberger.

He was 28, from Pennsylvania, and a graduate student at Washington State University, studying criminology. He owned a white Hyundai Elantra and lived in student housing at WSU, in the Pullman area.

Gary Jenkins, former chief of WSU Police Department, was asked to meet with the Moscow Police Department.

“They said, ‘We have a suspect who is a graduate student at Washington State University and his name is Bryan Kohberger,” he says.

“When they told me the name, it rang a bell but I didn’t immediately know why. It took me thirty seconds or so and then I said, ‘I’ve talked to Bryan Kohberger before. I interviewed him for a research assistant position at Pullman Police Department in April. I have his resume and his cover letter.’ Their ears pricked up.



“When I interviewed him, he was kind of an odd guy. Not enough to raise a red flag that he would go out and do something horrible. But his personality was a little bit off. I thought that he probably couldn’t relate well to people and I didn’t select him.”

During the course of their investigation into Kohberger, it became apparent that on 14 October 2022 – one month before the murders – a cop had pulled him over in his car for jumping a red light.

Bodycam footage of their conversation is shown in the documentary, revealing Kohberger’s, long, gaunt face and scary, bulging eyes.

A month after the murders, he was stopped again by traffic cops. This time on his way to his parents’ house in Pennsylvania, to spend the break there, accompanied by his father in the passenger seat.

This time, the offence was for driving too closely to the vehicle in front.



Police bodycam of this, too, was captured. Six weeks after the murders, police went to his parent’s house in Albrightsville, Pennsylvania, almost 3,000 miles away from Moscow, where they saw the white Hyundai Elantra.

It had almost been taken apart inside and had been scrubbed to

get rid of DNA. Police grabbed a rubbish bag from the kerb outside the house. Inside, they found a Q-tip which had some ear wax on it.

This provided them with a DNA sample which, one hundred per cent, had to be the father of their suspect. On 30 December 2022 they went back and arrested Bryan Kohberger.

During his police interview, Kohberger refused to answer any questions

Delving into his background, they learned that he was a loner, known to be sociallyawkward and disconcerted people by staring at them with his big, bulging blue eyes.

He invaded their space and was not very good at talking to women.



His master’s degree in criminal justice in Pennsylvania was under the tutelage of an expert in serial killers. He then moved to Washington to pursue a PhD in criminology and justice and, as part of his studies, he had been a teaching assistant at WSU.

But this ended after growing complaints about his behaviour and conduct towards women.

“Many people came forward to say he was a strange individual and off-putting, who thought very highly of themselves. Almost narcistic,” says Anthony Dahlinger.

“He would be very demeaning to others based on his level of education versus theirs.

“He had a lot of interest in people who had committed heinous crimes – serial killers, and the like.



“We learnt that he bought the knife and sheath off Amazon a couple of months before he moved to Washington. According to his digital footprint and his mobile ping, he had been in or around the area of the King Road house 23 times before the killings. It was always late in the evening or early morning between 10pm and 4am.”

Police found a disturbing selfie on his phone after he had driven home from the murders and scrubbed himself in the shower. It shows him smiling and giving a thumbs up to the camera.

In Idaho, he was facing the death penalty. He maintained his innocence and his defence team did all they could to delay the case and try to get it kicked out. Then he took a plea deal.

He pleaded guilty to all four murders and agreed to waive his appeal rights in exchange for avoiding the death penalty.

Kohberger has never given any reason why he carried out such atrocious murders.



“No one knows why he did it or whether he even knew them,” says Anthony.

“He had been in the area of the house, circling it, from as early as July 2022.”

On 23 July, 2025, he was given four consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole. He declined to make a statement himself and sat impassive during the victims’ family impact statements.

Looking across the courtroom at his daughter’s killer, Kaylee’s father, Steve

Goncalves, said, “In time, you will be forgotten to the wind. No visitors. Nothing more than initials on an unmarked tombstone.”

“Police officers tell us within minutes they had your DNA. Like a calling card. You were that careless. That foolish. That stupid masters degree? You’re a joke.”



Ben Mogen, Madison’s father, said she was much more than his only child.

“She was the only great thing I ever really did. And the only thing I was ever really proud of.”

He described struggling with addiction and substance abuse and how her daughter helped him.

“When I wasn’t wanting to live anymore, she was what would keep me from not caring.”

Scott Laramie, Madison’s stepfather, read a statement on behalf of him and her mother, Karen, saying their daughter was “Our gift of life, our purpose and our hope.”



Xana Kernodle’s stepfather, Randy Davis, told Kohberger, “You’re gonna go to hell … you’re evil … you took our children … you are gonna suffer, man.”

Ethan Chapin’s family chose not to attend the sentencing, saying they wanted to move on.

Bethany Funke wrote a statement, read aloud by a friend: “I hated and still hate that they are gone, but for some reason, I am still here, and I got to live,”

“Why did I get to live and not them? For the longest time, I could not even look at their families without feeling sick with guilt.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An emotional Dylan Mortensen, was in court and read out her statement in person: “He didn’t just take their lives, he took the light they carried into every room. He took away the ability for me to tell them that I love them and that I’m so proud of them.”



The Idaho Murders. Sky Crime, Sunday 26 July

News.title: Berlin Pride crash updates: Police hunt suspect as van ramming 'likely terror attack'
News.content:
Police in Berlin say a major manhunt is underway after a white minivan ploughed into a crowd of people in the Tiergarten park at around 10pm on Saturday night

German authorities have issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van ramming near Berlin's Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 25 others.

Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. They said he is believed to have injured several people with a moving vehicle late Saturday evening, and that one or more people apparently then left that vehicle. Several people were also apparently stabbed, they added.

Sunday's notice warned the public to avoid "direct contact" with the suspect, saying that he may be armed and dangerous.

Germany’s Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said initial findings suggest "we have experienced an Islamist terror attack".

News.title: Van deliberately driven into police officers in Scotland with suspect on the loose
News.content:
Van deliberately driven into police officers in Scotland with suspect on the loose

Police have launched an attempted murder investigation after two officers were injured when a van was deliberately driven at them in Larkhall on Saturday

View Image Officers were carrying out inquiries at a property on Glen Avenue when a white van was deliberately driven at them (Image: Google Maps)

Two police officers have been taken to hospital with serious injuries in a “deliberate and despicable attack” in Larkhall.

‌



Officers were carrying out inquiries at a property on Glen Avenue at about 2.10pm on Saturday when a white Renault Trafic van was deliberately driven at them in what police have called an attempted murder.

‌



Two male officers aged 43 and 41 were taken to hospital with serious injuries.

‌



The 41-year-old has since been released and the 43-year-old remains in hospital in a stable condition.

Police said there were no reports of any other injuries, and the van was later recovered in Kirkstyle Place, Glassford.

Detective Inspector Gary Smillie said: “This was a deliberate and despicable attack on two officers who were simply carrying out their duties.”

‌



Gatwick Airport left with no running water, working toilets or drinks READ MORE :

Police launched an attempted murder investigation and appealed for information.

The suspect is described as a white male, 6ft tall, wearing dark shorts, a grey jumper and a beige baseball cap.

Mr Smillie has asked anyone with dash cam footage or private CCTV which could help police to get in touch.

‌



He said: “Any information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, could assist with the investigation.”

Chief Inspector Paul Doyle added: “Violence is not part of the job for police officers – it is not acceptable and will not be tolerated.

“I would like to reassure the community that we are working to trace the person responsible and will continue to carry out inquiries in the local area.”

Article continues below

“We are speaking to members of the public and there will be additional patrols in the area, and would encourage anyone with any information or concerns to speak to officers.

“Our thoughts are with the officers, their families and colleagues at this time. We will continue to offer them all the necessary support.”

Anyone with any information should contact 101 quoting reference 1652 of 25 July, 2026. Information can also be given to Crimestoppers anonymously by calling 0800 555 111.

News.title: Ryanair flight declares mid-air emergency after taking off from Birmingham
News.content:
Ryanair flight declares mid-air emergency after taking off from Birmingham

The Ryanair flight departed Birmingham on what was expected to be a routine journey across the Irish Sea to Dublin, but was forced to make an emergency landing

View Image Crew members reported an emergency over the Irish Sea (stock) (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

A Ryanair flight was forced to declare an emergency shortly after taking off from Birmingham after a passenger reportedly suffered a medical emergency on board.

‌



Flight FR661, operated by a Boeing 737-800, departed Birmingham Airport at 08:37am on Sunday on what was expected to be a routine journey across the Irish Sea to Dublin.

‌



But as the aircraft began its descent towards the Irish capital, the crew issued the emergency squawk code 7700 - the universal transponder code used by pilots to declare a general emergency.

‌



According to flight tracking reports from AirLive, the aircraft was passing through around 8,000 feet over the Irish Sea when the emergency code was transmitted.

Air traffic controllers granted the flight priority landing clearance, with the aircraft touching down safely on Runway 28L at Dublin Airport around 40 minutes after departing Birmingham.

Article continues below

Emergency ground crews were on standby to meet the aircraft after it arrived at gate 109.

The emergency was reportedly declared following a medical incident involving a passenger.

The Mirror has contacted Ryanair for comment.

News.title: Bowls-playing pensioner William Eastment, 80, back in UK after South American drug smuggling nightmare
News.content:
Unrecognisable to his neighbours, the bowls-playing pensioner, once suspected of being an international drug smuggler, is pictured back in Britain a year trapped in a Chilean prison hell.

William Eastment was seen shuffling through his Somerset village, which he feared he would never see again, just days after the case against him was dropped. Anyone who did not know the 80-year-old, known to his pals as “Billy Boy”, would be forgiven for mistaking the frail pensioner for the international drugs courier he was accused of being.

His hollow cheeks, painfully thin frame and cautious steps bear little resemblance to the familiar bowls player who left Milborne Port last year. But Eastment was cleared after prosecutors accepted he had been duped by a sophisticated criminal gang.

View 4 Images William 'Billy Boy' Eastment, 80, looks frail and dramatically changed after returning to his Somerset village following a year trapped in a Chilean prison (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

‌



Berlin Pride crash updates: Police hunt suspect Abdul Ballout after van driven into crowd READ MORE :

Fake baby 'mother' Kira Cousins breaks silence on why she did it READ MORE :

The fraudsters tricked him into carrying a suitcase containing more than 5kg of methamphetamine. Eastment is now readjusting to ordinary life at his one-bedroom housing association bungalow. He is being supported by friends who feared his failing health meant he might never make it home.

The retired HGV and bus fitter has been seen cautiously venturing outside and taking short walks around his local area as he attempts to regain his strength. He was later spotted shopping in nearby Yeovil.

The trip marked another significant step in his recovery after months when every aspect of his life was controlled by prison guards and the Chilean courts. His dramatic weight loss has left him so changed that several people in the area are understood to have failed to recognise him.

View 4 Images Eastment after his arrest (Image: chilevision.cl)

‌



A neighbour said: “Billy has lost an incredible amount of weight and looks terribly frail. A few people have walked past without recognising him because he looks so different from before he left. He is moving very slowly, but his friends are rallying around him and helping him settle back into life at home. He’s been a bl**** fool, but everyone is relieved to see him back.”

Eastment’s return last week brings an extraordinary ordeal full circle after he was arrested at Santiago Airport on May 18 last year. He had arrived on a flight from Cancun, Mexico, carrying a suitcase allegedly containing Class A drugs worth around £200,000.

Chilean officials initially suspected the pensioner was an international drug courier. The Welshman was locked inside Santiago 1 Penitentiary, one of South America’s toughest prisons. Eastment insisted from the beginning that he had no idea the drugs were concealed inside the case.

View 4 Images Eastment was fit and healthy before the scam that turned his retirement into an international drugs nightmare.

‌



His nightmare began with an email claiming he was entitled to a $10.5million inheritance, worth around £7.85million. The message was part of an elaborate scam. Criminals used the name of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to convince him the fortune was genuine.

Eastment, who was living on his pension, was told a sponsor would pay for his flights and hotels in return for ten per cent of the supposed inheritance. The gang flew him around the world, including trips to Mexico and Japan. He was handed official-looking paperwork and told to sign documents.

By paying for hotels and allowing him time to go sightseeing, the criminals carefully built his trust. When the promised money failed to arrive, Eastment was told he needed to travel again to complete further paperwork. He was flown back to Mexico and given a suitcase, which he was instructed to take to New Zealand via Chile.

A woman allegedly told him it contained gifts for people associated with the IMF. Eastment could not open the case because it was secured with a combination lock. When customs officers stopped him at Santiago Airport, a border patrol worker eventually forced it open. Officers found oversized clothing inside. They then discovered the suspected drugs concealed beneath it.

‌



For months, Eastment faced the prospect of spending the rest of his life behind bars. While he was being held, his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease worsened in custody, and he suffered repeated bouts of pneumonia.

Investigators continued to examine the messages and evidence stored on Eastment’s phone and tablet.

View 4 Images The suitcase Eastment was tricked into carrying contained more than 5kg of methamphetamine, hidden beneath oversized clothing and worth around £200,000. (Image: Daily Mirror)

A police report concluded there was a high probability he had been scammed into travelling. The evidence supported his account. Prosecutors dismissed the proceedings, allowing him to return to Britain without facing trial, with officials arranging an emergency passport and helping organise his journey home.

News.title: Streeting says he wouldn't have accepted Defence Secretary job without Burnham spending promise
News.content:
Streeting says he wouldn't have accepted Defence Secretary job without Burnham spending promise

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would not have said yes to the new role without an assurance that enough cash was coming, as pressure mounts to say when defence spending will reach 3% of the national income

View 2 Images Wes Streeting was named as the new Defence Secretary on Monday (Image: Getty Images)

Wes Streeting has said he would not have accepted the Defence Secretary job if Andy Burnham had not convinced him that investment was coming.

‌



Mr Streeting said it is an advantage having his predecessor, John Healey, now heading the Treasury. Mr Healey needs to carve out billions of pounds in his first Budget to pay for the government's defence plans.

‌



Mr Streeting told Sky News: "If I didn't have confidence that this Prime Minister and this Chancellor would be investing in our defence sufficiently to protect our country, to protect our allies, and to meet our international commitments, then no, I wouldn't have taken the job.

‌



"But of the many things that I discussed with the Prime Minister before he took office and before I decided to support him to be leader of the Labour Party, I was absolutely assured of his commitment to our defense and security."

Streeting backs Burnham to sort out Britain's social care crisis with dig at Starmer READ MORE :

View 2 Images John Healey said he and Andy Burnham will make defence their top priority (Image: Simon Dawson / No 10 Downing Street)

He went on: "Next week, what you will see is a Prime Minister that runs towards big and difficult issues rather than runs away from them."

‌



One of the biggest issues to contend with will be defence spending. New Treasury chief Mr Healey dramatically quit Keir Starmer's government in June, accusing Mr Starmer and previous Chancellor Rachel Reeves of not putting aside enough cash to defend the nation.

The government is under pressure to ramp up spending on defence to 3% of national income, but has yet to set out a timetable to do so.

Mr Healey told The Sun that defence spending would be his first priority. He said: “I have argued for many years – and Andy Burnham has said the same – that the first duty of any government is to keep the country safe and protect our citizens.

‌



“That is fundamental to the way that I work in government and the decisions I take.” At the moment the UK's defence budget is expected to hit 2.7% of gross national product (GDP) by 2029.

But when he resigned as Defence Secretary on June 11, Mr Healey voiced his frustration that no timetable had been set out to reach 3%. Keir Starmer previously told Nato the figure would rise still further, to 3.5%, by 2035.

His successor has yet to set out his defence spending plans. But last week his official spokesman told reporters: "We will honour our commitments on defence to our international partners, and as I say, we’ll set out more on defence in due course.

Article continues below

“He told the Nato secretary-general (Mark Rutte) the appointment of John Healey as chancellor is a signal of his intent.”

In his first Budget, Mr Healey will need to find an extra £4.7billion to pay for the government's Defence Investment Plan (DIP), which was published on June 30. Documents released at the time said the sum would need to be set out in the Budget, meaning the Chancellor will be scrambling over the summer to find savings or raise taxes.

News.title: Met Office and BBC issue heatwave verdicts as UK weather maps show 38C surge
News.content:
Met Office and BBC issue heatwave verdicts as UK weather maps show 38C surge

Heatwave conditions are expected to return to the UK next week as weather forecasters at the Met Office and BBC say temperatures will rise back past 30C once more

View 2 Images Temperatures will surge well above the seasonal average next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

Weather forecasters for the BBC and Met Office say heatwave conditions will return to the UK next week.

‌



The BBC says highs of 35C are on the cards, with Wednesday expected to be the warmest day. East Wales and most of England will surge past 30C.

‌



Conditions are also expected to turn hotter than they have been in Northern Ireland and Scotland. Temperatures there could rise into the mid-20s, with the BBC adding: “Some computer models suggest an even more intense surge of heat could arrive by midweek.”

‌



The Met Office forecast suggests highs of 31C could come in southern areas on Tuesday, with 28C in northern regions. It predicts peak temperatures of 32C for Wednesday and 30C for Thursday.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Met Office names areas facing rain on Monday as 49 counties set for wet weather READ MORE :

UK weather model shows 45C heat surge in what would be hottest day ever seen READ MORE :

Some weather models show temperatures could rise as high as 38C on Wednesday - which would be the hottest day of the year so far. The GFS model shows those highs coming in eastern parts of England, with 37C in the Midlands and parts of Yorkshire too.

‌



Anomaly maps for next week show most of the UK shaded in red and black. This indicates that temperatures are expected to rise well above the seasonal average.

View 2 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Wednesday (Image: WXCHARTS)

How long will the heatwave last?

According to the BBC, forecasts suggest conditions will turn cooler again by next weekend as Atlantic systems bring rain and westerly winds.

Article continues below

The BBC says: “How long the heat lasts depends on whether a southerly or westerly wind develops. A westerly wind will bring an end to heatwave conditions, while southerly winds could signal a return to intense heat.”

The Met Office expects southern regions to “remain relatively settled and very warm” towards the end of July and at the start of August.

“Northern parts of the UK could still see some periods of rain or showers,” the national weather agency said. “Early August could see a change to more widely unsettled conditions, but details of this are very uncertain at this stage.”

News.title: Dying mum raises more than £50,000 to spend more time with her children
News.content:
Dying mum raises more than £50,000 to spend more time with her children

Jess Duggan sends message to the NHS after crowdfunding Enhertu treatment

A dying mum has managed to raise more than £50,000 thanks to the public after appealing in the Mirror for the NHS to fund the life-extending Enhertu drug.

‌



Jess Duggan, 44, said she has been touched by the “incredible outpouring of humanity, ” which she described as “mind-blowing.” After raising funds to pay for the drug privately, she has now had her first infusion and has celebrated her daughter's sweet 16th and is now desperately hoping to see her son's 13th in September.

‌



We told how the Enhertu drug is being denied Jess and thousands of other women with breast cancer in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, yet it is free in Scotland and 26 other European countries. Jess says the money raised for her treatment shows how the public feel about this 'cruel' decision.

‌



View 2 Images Jess Duggan is fighting for vital time with her husband and children

These are the faces of dozens of tragic Brits who lost their lives in open water READ MORE :

A recent poll by Breast Cancer Now revealed 82 per cent of UK adults believe the life-extending drug should be made available to those who need it on the NHS.

The mum, who has breast cancer which has spread to her brain and her liver, recently had the agonising task of telling her children she only had six weeks left to live. “They are feeling very angry they are being deprived of their mum because the drug is not an option on the NHS,” she told The Mirror.

‌



Despite her pain, Jess, from Lewes, is bravely campaigning for the drug to be made available on the NHS, said of the crowdfunding success: “There are so many lovely people. I don’t know who they are. There are so many generous family and friends, they just blow my mind. There are people saying ‘I don’t know who you are but here is some money’. They don’t even know me!

“It ’s been a really heartwarming thing to go through in really dark times. You see this incredible outpouring of humanity and generosity and it shows what the public think about this drug and how it should be paid for.”

View 2 Images Jess Duggan says the decision not to fund a life-prolonging drug on the NHS was 'cruel'

‌



She is now urging the new Health Secretary Yvette Cooper to have a “brilliant” start to her latest cabinet role by putting on the pressure for the drug to be funded by the NHS. So far it has been turned down as it is too expensive.

Jess was given a six week prognosis on July 1st this year, prompting her decision to ask the public for help pay for the drug, which has been proven to prolong life for six months.

“It’s horrible asking people for money but I had just been given the awful news I had six weeks to live,” she told The Mirror. “My friends put an appeal for help on social media and it went live and thank God for them, the money then started coming in. We had a couple of quite big anonymous donations, one for £12,000.

‌



“Now we’ve raised £50,000 which is enough for five doses because you not only have to pay for the drug but also the nursing, the pharmacy, the oncology equipment and all those associated costs that come with it. It’s not much change from £10,000 per round.

“I’ve had one so far and fingers crossed it’s all working. Optimistically things feel a big stable." She said after being given the devastating diagnosis she was offered a chemo treatment which had a five per cent chance of helping and then only for a few weeks.

"It was very much ‘this is hospice time’. It’s really hard for the doctors because they cannot suggest Enhertu to you because they can’t offer it. So it is up to the patient to say ‘what about Enhertu and I can crowd fund’."

‌



When she did ask them, they said: ‘Yep we’ve discussed it and it’s your best option if you’ve got the money'. They’ve worked really hard because it's not that easy to go private, you've got to find a doctor and hospital willing to do it," she explained.

“We have been fortunate that we have had some really lovely people really working on our side with the fundraising and getting access to the drug.”

About celebrating her daughter’s 16th recently, she said: “Everything went well, she had a Prom, she enjoyed everything with no health dramas but it was a shame a week later we had to deliver this news.

‌



“I think it’s fair to say my children are very angry with the Government because this drug is not available. If this drug had been available to me four treatments ago I would be in such a different position, I wouldn’t have the widespread level of cancer I’ve got that this drug has to try and beat.

“The six week tightrope is still very threatening, as it really has got to bring me back from the brink and it's whether it is capable at this point. Although I am still optimistic it will give me more time. We will only know if it works if I’m alive or not. We are not waiting to do scans, It’s if my liver doesn’t fail. That’s the reality the Government has put me in

“They just keep giving out the same wishy-washy statement while people are dying. Where is their sense of urgency? And imagine if it does work well for me but what do I do in five cycles? Do I just keep begging for money, do I sell my house?

‌



“What kind of decisions do I have to make around the financial future of my family? It’s just a horrible position to be in. And the drug is there and it’s available. It’s mad. just crazy.”

Helen Dickens chief support officer at Breast Cancer Now says: "It’s heartbreaking that Enhertu remains out of reach for people with incurable metastatic breast cancer like Jess, robbing them of the chance of precious extra time to live.

"No one should have to rely on crowdfunding to access a life-extending treatment that could give them more time with their loved ones...And sadly, Jess isn’t the only one.

‌



"Since it was rejected for use on the NHS in England two years ago (in 2024), thousands of people with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer have missed out on this vital life-extending drug, and sadly many have already died.

"Jess and thousands of other people living with incurable metastatic breast cancer, should be spending their precious time left with loved ones, making priceless memories, not campaigning for access to a drug that is already available in Scotland and 25 other European countries.

"Our petition alongside METUPUK and Make 2nds Count, has already been signed by over 68,000 people. It’s demanding all four parties urgently reach a deal and finally make Enhertu available for those who need it."People with metastatic breast cancer do not have time to wait, they need Enhertu now."

‌



When approached the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) said 'Enhertu for Her-2 low metastatic breast cancer "remains the only breast cancer treatment NICE has been unable to recommend for patients, in the last eight years.

"This was because, at the price offered by the company, in 2024, the treatment was too expensive for the benefits it provided, and NICE concluded it was not cost effective.

"As part of the US-UK trade deal, announced in December 2025, NICE is now using a new higher threshold for cost effectives decisions.

‌



"Given these new circumstances, discussions involving NICE, the companies and NHS England have resumed to try to seek agreement on a commercial offer that would make Enhertu cost effective. NICE stands ready to consider reviewing the guidance if new evidence, including a new commercial offer, were to be put forward by the company.

"NICE remains committed to getting the best care to patients and we understand the impact this decision has had on the breast cancer community. "

A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "Our deepest sympathies go out to Jess Duggan and all those impacted by breast cancer.

Article continues below

"Decisions on approving treatments for NHS use are taken by the independent body NICE. As part of the US-UK trade arrangement, NICE is now using a new higher cost-effectiveness threshold, allowing discussions with manufacturers of Enhertu to resume."

News.title: Weight loss injection side effects truth that everyone taking Wegovy, Mounjaro or Ozempic should be aware of
News.content:
Originally designed to tackle diabetes, weight loss injections such as Wegovy and Mounjaro are now being taken by 2.4 million Brits.

Experts have hailed them as a wonder drug, helping people drop as much as a fifth of their body weight – as well as other benefits from preventing heart attacks and cancer to tackling addiction and depression.

While the drugs, which mimic a hormone called glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) to suppress appetite, are safe for use on the NHS, side effects are still emerging. This week scientists published research suggesting a link between weight-loss jabs and hair loss, while patients regularly report issues with vomiting and diarrhea.

Here are the side effects – and the scientific evidence behind them – to look out for:

‌



View 10 Images You can't just eat less of the same junk food (Image: PA)

Warning as Wegovy pill goes on sale in Britain for the first time from today READ MORE :

Gym influencer who sells weight loss jabs on social media unmasked as convicted drug dealer READ MORE :

Malnutrition

Suddenly reducing how much you eat is a drastic change which needs to be properly managed. Earlier this year Europe’s biggest obesity conference in Istanbul issued a “consensus statement” warning that users of GLP-1 drugs will become malnourished if they continue with junk food diets, but just eat less of it.

The document, co-authored by 26 top obesity experts, outlined how it is vital that jab users eat enough quality protein. Co-author Dr Laurence Dobbie, population health expert at King’s College London, said: “To protect dietary quality we need to prioritise nutrient-dense foods, ensuring appropriate protein, fibre and fluid intake.”

Hair Loss

New research published this week suggests weight loss drugs could cause your hair to fall out. People on the appetite-suppressing meds have been reporting hair loss to regulators but it was not known whether it was being caused by the drugs themselves.

‌



View 10 Images Alopecia is being investigated as a potential side effect (Image: Getty Images)

A study of 50,000 users of weight loss jabs, such as Wegovy and Mounjaro, appears to confirm a link between them and a rare side effect of alopecia. Although the overall risk is low, analysis of electronic patient data from the US showed patients on weight loss drugs were 68% more likely to report hair loss than comparable patients on different diabetes medications.

Experts believe it could be caused by sudden drops in calorie intake and nutrient deficiencies. The US Food and Drug Administration is now investigating the possible side effect.

Tummy Troubles

The most commonly reported side effects of weight loss injections are nausea and vomiting. Other issues are diarrhea and constipation while some users report stomach cramps, indigestion and bloating.

‌



The NHS advises drinking plenty of fluids - 2-3 litres daily - to stay hydrated if you experience diarrhea. While for many these side effects can be relatively minor, for some they are bad enough that they have to stop taking the medication.

View 10 Images Diarrhea is a known side effect (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Rare but severe side effects reported include people needing to have their gallbladders removed and acute pancreatitis which can be fatal.

Wrinkles

Losing a lot of weight can lead to one obvious side effect - excess skin. While this is often considered a price worth paying for the wider health benefits of weight loss, it had led to reports of “Ozempic face”, “Ozempic feet” and even “Ozempic butt”.

‌



This has been highlighted among celebrities who have been open about taking the medication and refers to a sagging or aging of the skin. Sharon Osbourne has spoken about using Ozempic for weight loss and said she started taking the injections in late 2022 but stopped more recently.

View 10 Images Sharon Osbourne has spoken about using Ozempic (Image: WireImage)

Ozempic face refers to a sunken or hollowed out appearance the face can take on after drastic weight loss. It can also increase signs of ageing including lines and wrinkles. This happens because GLP-1 drugs are not localised to act only on the fat people want to lose.

It targets all of our body’s fat – including in the face. Dr Barry Weintraub, a New York-based board certified plastic surgeon, has spoken about how a loss of fat can impact water retention in the body and cause excessive sagging in the feet.

‌



Bad Breath

Bad breath - known officially as halitosis - is a reported side effect of weight loss jabs but there is not yet peer-reviewed data on this. Some experts suspect that reduced appetite means people drink less water contributing to dry mouth.

This can lead to an overgrowth of bacteria such as Streptococcus, Lactobacillus and Porphyromonas gingivalis which can contribute to odours. In one study run by Novo Nordisk nearly 9% of people taking semaglutide - the main component of Ozempic and Wegovy - reported increased burping.

View 10 Images Users have reported halitosis (Image: Getty Images)

Tooth Damage

One of the major side-effects of Ozempic is vomiting. Adam Taylor, professor of anatomy at Lancaster University, has explained how these drugs slow how quickly the stomach empties, delaying digestion which can lead to bloating, nausea and vomiting.

‌



Repeated vomiting can damage the teeth because stomach acid erodes the enamel of the teeth. This damage is permanent.

View 10 Images Stomach acid can damage teeth (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Professor Taylor recommends that if users get sick, not to immediately brush their teeth. Instead he advises people to rinse the mouth out with water or mouthwash to reduce the strength of the acid and wait at least 30 minutes before brushing.

Pile the Pounds Back On

Oxford University scientists established that people generally pile the pounds back on within a year of stopping weight loss jabs.

‌



They analysed 11 studies involving 6,370 adults on the appetite-suppressing injections and found they typically lost 8kg - but returned to their original weight within 10 months of stopping. It suggested that many users need to be on the powerful drugs for life.

Many patients give up the treatment either because they can no longer afford the private prescriptions, because they decide the side effects such as vomiting are too much, or they are not losing weight anymore.

View 10 Images Many users put the weight back on (Image: Getty Images)

Co-author Prof Susan Jebb, of Oxford University, said: “Either people really have to accept this as a treatment for life, you’re going to have to keep going forever, or we in science need to think really, really hard, how to support people when they stop the drug.”

‌



Bone and Muscle Mass

Almost a third of pounds shed from weight loss jabs is actually muscle and bone density. Scientists who uncovered this research have stressed that it is vital people change their lives and do exercise while losing weight on the jabs to sustain it in the long term.

Their review of 21 studies included data from high tech scanners which assessed where weight was being lost from on the body. It showed that of the weight lost after taking jabs, 31.5% of it was “fat free mass” such as muscle and bone density. This compared to 14.3% for people who lost weight through diet and exercise alone.

Other studies have shown that if people stop taking the drugs they pile the fat back on - but the muscle and bone mass is lost for good. This makes it much harder to lose weight again because there is less muscle to burn calories. It also increases the chances of osteoporosis and frailty in old age.

View 10 Images Resistance training is essential, experts say (stock) (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



The secret, it seems, is to do weight bearing exercises while taking GLP-1 drugs. This could involve press-ups, pull-ups, squats or lifting weights.

Dr Laurence Dobbie said: “The primary, most crucial component is resistance training, aiming for two to three bouts per week. Secondary to this is 150 to 300 minutes a week of aerobic exercise… all movement is beneficial.”

What does the NHS say?

The NHS stresses that you'll need to eat a balanced diet with fewer calories and do regular physical activity while taking weight loss drugs. All GLP-1 medicines are prescription only medicines, which means they can only be prescribed by a healthcare professional.

They should come with personalised behavioral, nutritional, and psychological support including diet and exercise plans. However the quality of this accompanying support service can vary and this can be the difference between sustained weight loss or eventually piling it back on.

‌



Fake GLP-1 drugs bought from unregulated sellers - such as beauty salons or via social media - have caused severe side effects. Health chiefs insist none should be purchased with a consultation with a healthcare professional.

View 10 Images The NHS only prescribes GLP-1s with personalised support (Image: PA)

An estimated 2.4 million Brits are taking weight-loss jabs but the vast majority are having to pay privately for them because the NHS does not yet have the resources to offer them to everyone who is technically eligible.

The NHS prescribes the weekly injections Mounjaro and Wegovy for weight loss but Ozempic only for diabetes. NHS chiefs say they are prioritising prescriptions for the most in need, so are offering them to the severely obese who also suffer from a range of other health problems.

‌



The rollout of Mounjaro was announced by NHS England with much fanfare in 2024 but an investigation by the British Medical Journal (BMJ) a year later revealed how the jabs were being rationed. Some 3.4 million people are technically eligible for the jabs but the NHS planned a phased rollout over a 12-year period.

Health Minister Sharon Hodgson said: “Weight loss drugs are proving to be a game changer in tackling obesity. We are committed to ensuring the NHS makes these drugs available to those who need them most.”

News.title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
News.content:
Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."

Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."

Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".

Responding to Burnham's comments, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: "Clearly, the US is a long standing ally. We need to have good relations with them but if they do something we disagree with, we should honestly say so."

The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.

But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that.

"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
News.content:
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, Andy Burnham explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election, saying "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it."

Explaining his decision, the new prime minister suggested the majority of the electorate "voted for a manifesto" in the last election, and vowed he would "honour that manifesto" with the support of parliamentary colleagues.

Burnham went on to say, "I just think what I most need to do is get Britain focused on getting the country back where it should be, getting it working."

Andy Burnham: The Laura Kuenssberg Interview will be available across BBC News on Sunday and the interview will be shown in full on Panorama on BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

News.title: Gatwick Airport left without running water after major outage
News.content:
Passengers at both terminals of Gatwick Airport are being affected by a water supply issue, with toilets reported to be out of order and restaurants closed.

In a statement on X, the airport in West Sussex apologised for the disruption, external and said a problem in the Horley area was affecting supplies and was under investigation.

Bottled water is being made available to passengers and staff and contingency measures have also been put in place, it said.

SES Water, which covers the airport, has said its Bough Beech water treatment works was back up and running after an earlier power outage, but it still needs to treat the water before returning supplies.

The company, which also supplies parts of Kent, Surrey and south London, said complications caused by a power outage at the treatment works meant some customers had experienced low water pressure or a temporary loss of supply.

A spokesperson had earlier confirmed that Gatwick Airport was affected.

In an update just before 13:45 BST, they said: "Our Bough Beech water treatment works are back up and running.

"We now need to treat the water before returning services to normal as quickly as we possibly can."

Gatwick said the supply issue was continuing to cause disruption on Sunday afternoon.

In a statement, it said: "There is currently no water supply in either terminal.

"Our staff are on hand to support passengers and provide assistance where needed, some restaurant partners have opened to provide additional seating."

The airport said it was working closely with the water company to restore supplies as quickly as possible.

News.title: Meghan calls Harry 'a charmer' during MasterChef Australia appearance
News.content:
Early on in the episode, Meghan was asked what her favourite dish is to make at home.

She said it was "a tough one because I have a lot of palettes to appease", with her British-born husband favouring "meat, potatoes and cream sauce" while she preferred grilled fish.

Their two children, Archie and Lilibet, often help with meal preparation and are "great eaters", she said.

"We're really lucky on that front," she added.

She then urged the chefs to cook something they felt connected to. "What's the story behind it?" she asked them.

When Prince Harry dialled in later on during the episode, Meghan told them: "My husband's here," prompting cheers and shocked faces from contestants and spectators.

"I wish you could try these, these dishes are fantastic," she told him, before showing him the food. He signed off by telling her to go and enjoy, adding: "Very sorry to disturb you."

The duchessâs appearance on the latest season of the show was well received by Hello Magazine, external, which shared a video of the episode online and complimented Meghan for the way she interacted with the chefs.

"The Duchess of Sussex gave personal time calls to all the contestants, proving that she's always so effortlessly elegant," it wrote.

Writing in The Sunday Times, external, Charlotte Ivers was less impressed, saying her appearance on the show "told us nothing about what she likes or who even will leave the competition".

Social media users were also split, with one viewer writing that Meghan was "warm, gracious and a delight to watch" while another called Prince Harry's cameo appearance "cringe".

News.title: Primark's new 'supermarket tactic' to woo customers in online price war
News.content:
"Primark isn't as cheap any more."

It is something I keep hearing shoppers say when I ask them whether they shop at the fast-fashion giant.

"It's definitely got more expensive," says 19-year-old student Eshal Malik as she browses the jewellery at Primark with a friend.

But that might be about to change. Primark said on Monday that it was lowering prices on hundreds of clothing items, including jeans, jumpers and socks.

"It's the kind of headline you'd expect from M&S or Next," says retail analyst Natalie Berg, explaining that price cuts like this from such a low-cost retailer are surprising.

"You don't want to join a race to the bottom," she says. "But when Shein is selling dresses for Â£3, you've got to respond, right?"

Primark, which has more than 190 UK stores, has been experiencing a drop in like-for-like sales, a key measure in the retail industry.

Increases to the price of fabric, minimum wages, shipping and energy costs and a focus on higher standards overall has contributed to the rising price of clothes for the likes of Primark in recent years.

The announcement of price cuts comes ahead of parent company Associated British Foods' plan to spin off the business onto the London stock market next year.

The level of competition among fashion retailers has "evolved dramatically" over the past few years, and Chinese online marketplaces Shein and Temu are now competing for Primark's customers, says Berg.

But there is also competition from other online retailers like TikTok Shop and Vinted, she says.

By slashing prices on some core items, Primark is likely hoping to woo shoppers with low-cost staples, in the same way that supermarkets attract customers with cheap milk and bananas, Berg says.

News.title: I thought the Lockerbie bombing was a closed case until I started asking questions
News.content:
I was only a year old when the UK's deadliest terror attack shocked the world.

In December 1988, Pan Am flight 103 exploded - killing all 259 people on board as well as 11 on the ground in the Scottish town of Lockerbie.

I was a teenager by the time Libyan intelligence officer Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was convicted of the bombing in 2001 and, when he later died, I thought that was largely the end of the story.

It wasn't.

The case still rumbles on and, later this year, a man suspected of making the bomb which blew up the plane, Abu Agila Masud, goes on trial in Washington DC.

As part of a Radio 4 Intrigue podcast series, I had an opportunity to delve into this complex case with fresh eyes.

The deeper I dug, the more complicated Lockerbie became and there have been times that I don't know what to believe.

News.title: Pizza, pasta, potatoes, protein - how Italian children became so overweight
News.content:
Daily life is not easy for Salvatore. At 17, he weighs 170kg (26st 10lb) and struggles to walk.

He can't tie his own shoelaces and his Vespa scooter strains to bear his weight - in one week, its wheels broke seven times.

"He eats constantly," says his mother Anna.

Salvatore is among a growing number of Italian children and teenagers living with obesity. The problem is particularly acute in the south: in parts of the Campania region, more than 40% of eight and nine-year-olds are overweight. The town of Ponticelli, on the outskirts of Naples, has earned the unenviable reputation as one of the world's child obesity capitals.

It is a striking development in a country long regarded as the spiritual home of the Mediterranean diet. Yet today, Italian children are among the most overweight in Europe, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Salvatore is waiting for life-changing surgery at the Betania Hospital in Ponticelli, where Dr Sonja Chiappetta has spent 15 years treating patients with severe obesity.

Until recently, she says, most of her patients were in their fifties. "Now I see those same patients when they're teenagers, as young as 16. They are getting younger, and it's frightening."

The surgery she carries out removes up to 90% of the stomach - meaning people are unable to eat large quantities of food. Demand has risen sharply in this part of Italy.

But Salvatore has been told he cannot get the operation. His weight is so excessive it makes the surgery too dangerous.
