Instead, Dr Chiappetta has prescribed him a GLP-1 weight-loss injection to reduce his appetite and help him lose enough weight for the operation.

News.title: What Love Island tells us about the changing face of dating
News.content:
On the fourth series of Love Island UK in 2018, Megan Barton-Hanson pulled fellow Islander, Wes Nelson, for a chat.

Just moments earlier, she had ended her relationship with Eyal Booker after admitting the pair had little more than physical chemistry. Now, sitting opposite Wes, who had been coupled up with Laura Anderson since the start of the competition, she decided not to wait for him to make the first move.

"I think it's pretty obvious that I do really fancy you," she told him. "And I just felt like, if I didn't say something, I'd regret it massively."

By the end of the episode, viewers had a new nickname for her: "Muggy Megan". Critics accused her of moving too quickly between relationships and breaking "girl code". Others admired her honesty.

At the time, Barton-Hanson argued that she had been treated differently to her male counterparts. "People definitely do give girls a harder time than menâ¦ It's sexist."

But eight years later, scenes like Barton-Hanson's no longer feel quite so out of the ordinary. Until this series, the opening coupling had always seen the men choose first. This year, the show's rules were changed, with the women making the first choice.

News.title: Iran's 'sabre-rattling' should not intimidate UK, Wes Streeting says
News.content:
When asked if Iran had the capability to attack the UK, Streeting said: "I think we shouldn't put too much stock in the sabre-rattling of Iran, and we certainly shouldn't be intimidated by what the regime has said this week".

He also repeated the UK's position from the outset of the US war against Iran saying "we have not joined and will not join offensive US military action in Iran.

"That's an area where we have not agreed with the United States, but when it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the straight Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned".

Streeting said he is to meet with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth in the coming week after "kicking around" ideas for ways "to bring the countries together" and had been "delighted" to speak to Hegseth by phone already.

He also said that the UK is ready to lead a naval mission to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz "when the conditions are right".

Securing safe shipping routes through the area was important because of the impact the crisis is having on energy prices and the cost of living, he added.

Streeting also dismissed a Russian warship's recent live-firing exercise in the English Channel as "performative" but added it was a "reminder of the frankly unsafe and unprofessional way in which they have been conducting themselves".

Branding the Channel incident "irresponsible", Streeting said Russia posed a threat to UK security, adding that the public does not see "the enormous efforts that take place every day to counter Russian aggression".

News.title: Another UK heatwave looms after cooler end to weekend
News.content:
Sunday will be a cooler day for the whole of the UK as temperatures fall widely by a couple of degrees.

A few locations will finally mark the end to their third heatwave of the year, including Usk in Monmouthshire and Exeter in Devon.

Both places are forecast to see temperatures drop beneath the heatwave threshold for the first time in 21 consecutive days.

Temperatures will largely be in the mid-20s Celsius for the south-east of the UK and in the mid-teens Celsius further north.

For many, the relief from the heat will be short-lived as high pressure is set to build close to the south of the UK next week.

This will stall rain-bearing weather fronts and any wet weather will become confined to northern and western areas - especially north-west Scotland.

In southern parts of the UK, temperatures look set to climb once again.

Tapping into the heat over the near continent, the UK is likely to enter another heatwave, with temperatures in England and Wales forecast to peak around 25-32C for much of next week.

Yellow heat health alerts will come into effect for Yorkshire and Humber, the West and East Midlands, the East of England, London, south-east and south-west, at 9:00 BST on 28 July 2026 and last until 9:00 BST on 31 July.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

News.title: What a week's work experience taught these Year 10s about their futures
News.content:
When Kelsey first arrived at secondary school, she said she wanted to be almost anywhere else but there.

She struggled with friendships, clashed with teachers and often tried to avoid coming into school.

But after a week's work experience placement at Whipsnade Zoo, in Bedfordshire, her outlook could not be more different.

She said it made her a "completely different person" - more confident, with a "good group of friends" and a greater sense of purpose about where her education could lead her.

Children across the UK are strongly encouraged to do work experience while at school. In England, the government published new legal guidance in June for schools to deliver two weeks of "in-person and immersive" work experience in future, one between Year 7 and Year 9, and one between Years 10 and 11.

But not all work experience placements are equal, and finding the right one can be tricky.

Organisations like the Sutton Trust and the Social Mobility Foundation said some students could be limited by the availability of placements in their area, or a lack of family connections with local employers.

BBC News spoke to three Year 10 pupils, one year ahead of their final GCSE exams, about how they decided what areas of work they were interested in, their experiences of trying to find the right placement, and what it taught them about their future education and ultimate career goals.

News.title: Residents allowed to return after Cairngorms wildfire evacuation
News.content:
Residents of the village of Nethy Bridge, near the wildfire that has been burning in the Cairngorms, have been told they can return to their homes after being evacuated on Friday night.

The fire was declared a major incident due to a change in weather, but that has now been stood down by Police Scotland.

First Minister John Swinney said the government and emergency services will continue to treat the blaze with the utmost seriousness until the last flames are out.

Locals have criticised the handling of the wildfire, which has been burning for 10 days, saying the move to declare it a major incident came too late and the government had been slow in scaling up their response.

In a statement on Saturday night, Police Scotland said "after an extensive multi-agency response to a large fire within Cairngorms National Park, residents of Nethy Bridge are being advised that they can now return to their properties".

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service's deputy assistant chief officer, Kenny Barbour, said the decision to stand down the major incident followed a detailed assessment by emergency responders.

He added in a statement: "The extensive work carried out over recent days, including the creation of effective fire breaks, has significantly reduced the risk to nearby communities, allowing evacuated residents to safely return home."

Supt Judy Hill added that the "ongoing multi agency response remains a high priority, with significant partnership resources and volunteers working tirelessly and in challenging circumstances, to support our efforts to extinguish the fires".

Firefighters will continue to maintain a significant operational presence until the incident is safely concluded, with 75 remaining on the ground on Saturday, police said.

At a meeting of the Scottish government's resilience room on Saturday evening, the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said there had been "good progress" in strengthening fire breaks to protect residential areas and said the number of fire hot spots was reducing.

First Minister John Swinney welcomed the lifting of the evacuation notice but stressed that "the Scottish Government, the emergency services and all relevant authorities will continue to treat this wildfire, as has been the case since its onset, with the utmost seriousness and necessary resources until the last flames are out."

News.title: Man in critical condition after sea rescue
News.content:
A man is in a critical condition in hospital after three people got into difficulty in the water near an Essex pier.

Emergency services were called to an incident at Clacton-on-Sea shortly after 16:30 BST on Saturday.

A man aged in his 50s is in a critical but stable condition, Essex Police said.

Two other people, a man aged in his 20s and a teenage girl, remain in hospital but are "recovering well", the force added.

All three people knew each other.

News.title: 'It was like a movie - I looked up and an exploded barn rained on me'
News.content:
The photographer was driving to his studio for a meeting when he realised the fire on the horizon was at the farm where it was based.

"It was about 150 metres (492ft) from my front door, and I quickly cancelled the meeting and thought, 'I'm not happy with where the wind is going on this'," he said.

Johnson began removing some of his more expensive kit from the studio and was putting it in the van when the explosion took place.

A unit housing fertiliser had exploded.

He said: "It blew me into the door and I just ran to the van, dropped the bit I went back in for - maybe it saved my life, I don't know."

As it happened: Twenty firefighters taken to hospital after major Essex explosion

The photographer was shocked to see his studio roof had completely caved in.

Having driven to a safe distance, "I pulled over, and I was just in shock and started to shake", he said, although he was reassured after an ambulance crew checked him over.

Johnson managed to cover his wedding booking on Saturday, praising his "amazing assistant" James Musselwhite for driving from Portsmouth to help him out.

"I'm in a little bit of shock still, to be honest," he said.

"I'm completely unscathed apart from a bit of a dodgy ear from the pressure - but how I've got away with it unscathed I have no idea."

News.title: Tourists describe their escape from France wildfires
News.content:
Families have relived how their tranquil holidays in France turned into a race to escape raging wildfires.

Tourists told the BBC of emergency alerts in the middle of the night, desperate drives just metres from six-storey high flames and the sight of people flocking to beaches with their suitcases.

Huge forest fires in south-west France and central Spain have displaced more than 220,000 people, with the French military drafted in to help and the Spanish government declaring a national emergency.

Winds and continued heat are still helping to fan the flames with some tourists reporting smelling acrid smoke like a "bonfire" far outside the affected areas.

Flights to Bordeaux and Madrid, the closest cities to the blaze-hit regions, are currently not affected. Earlier on Saturday, a French foreign minister described the fires as a "tragedy" but urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans.

Among those caught up in the crisis is Zac Morrison, who arrived in Cap Ferret - a popular peninsula blanketed with pine trees 40 miles (65km) south-west of Bordeaux - on Thursday.

The 21-year-old from London, who is on holiday with 10 members of his family, woke up to two text alerts at 04:00 and 06:00 local time ordering him to evacuate "by all means necessary".

News.title: Man charged with possession of explosive substance after bomb found in car
News.content:
A Dublin museum employee has been charged in connection with an investigation into the discovery of a bomb in a car in the Republic of Ireland.

Simon O'Donovan, 44, with an address at Sperrin Road in Dublin 12, was charged with being in possession of an explosive substance at St Lawrence Rd in Chapelizod, Dublin 10 on 22 July.

He appeared before the Special Criminal Court on Saturday evening, where the court heard he was employed by the Collins Barracks National Museum of Ireland.

A vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross near the Irish border on Wednesday. On Friday, a 25-year-old woman was charged in relation to the same incident.

News.title: F1 Hungarian GP LIVE: Race updates as Piastri leads after Russell’s nightmare start
News.content:
Norris happy to be back on pole in Hungary

Lando Norris landed the first pole position of his world championship defence after he beat Lewis Hamilton to top spot for the Hungarian Grand Prix by just 0.012 seconds.

Hamilton appeared on course to end a three-year run without taking pole only to be usurped by Norris in the closing moments of a thrilling qualifying session at the Hungaroring.

It seemed like Hamilton had to settle for second, a place ahead of his team-mate Charles Leclerc, until he was docked three places by the stewards for impeding Oscar Piastri in what looked like a slam-dunk incident.

But he still has a strong chance of taking a record-extending ninth win at a venue he has so often ruled, and slash Kimi Antonelli’s advantage at the summit of the world championship standings - who was also hit with a three-place grid penalty after qualifying.

Follow live updates from the Hungarian GP with The Independent

News.title: ‘So his torture starts all over again’: Man who stole phone 14 years ago being returned to prison without release date
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A father who was convicted of a mobile phone robbery 14 years ago is being returned to prison on an indefinite jail term described as “psychological torture”.

Thomas White, 43, previously set himself alight in desperation as his mental health crumbled over the open-ended sentence, which has been condemned by the United Nations (UN).

Last October, his family won a six-year fight for him to be transferred to a medium secure hospital for treatment. They have now learned he will be returned to a category B prison “any day” after just nine months of care.

His sister, Pastor Clara White, fears his mental health will rapidly deteriorate back in prison without a release date, adding: “So his torture starts all over again.”

He was handed a controversial Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence for street robbery of a mobile phone in 2012. A judge told him he must serve a minimum of two years, but he has now been incarcerated for 14 years and four months, his family say.

open image in gallery Thomas White is being returned to prison from hospital, his family says ( Margaret White )

The open-ended punishments were scrapped in 2012, but not retrospectively, leaving thousands languishing in prison without a release date for years beyond their tariff, including some for minor crimes. Once released, many find themselves trapped in a cycle of indefinite recall for minor breaches of strict licence conditions.

White’s plight has formed part of a major complaint to the UN, which resulted in three special rapporteurs last week warning Britain is perpetrating “serious human rights violations” by failing to resentence almost 2,400 still trapped on the jail term.

A further 207 are serving their sentence in a secure hospital, often after their mental health deteriorated in prison, and 96 people have taken their own lives in custody.

In a strongly worded intervention, the UN said the jail terms have left prisoners trapped in a cycle of “excessive punishment, repeated recall, deteriorating mental health, and diminishing hope”.

“These penalties involve prolonged uncertainty and cause serious psychological deterioration among prisoners, including an increased risk of self-harm and suicide. Such punishments may amount to psychological torture,” the human rights experts added.

open image in gallery Pastor Clara White and Lord David Blunkett, who has said he regrets bringing in IPP sentences under Tony Blair ( White family )

Pastor White had long campaigned for her brother’s transfer to the unit in Northumberland – backed by The Independent – after he endured repeated mental health crises in prison, including setting himself alight and smashing his face on the cell floor.

After being told he would go back to prison, she told The Independent: “It’s like he’s just had a bit of respite and that’s about it.”

She continued: “Thomas will get very poorly very quickly when sent back, because he hasn’t improved, he’s maybe slightly better.

“I don’t think nine months is enough for a man to unravel and to start trusting and start speaking.

“So you punish a man because he’s not fitting into your timescale of how long he should be there. So his torture starts all over again.”

His transfer back to prison will mark his 14th move in as many years after he was repeatedly transferred to prisons across the country.

Doctors at the secure unit have concluded White has a number of mental health conditions.

However two medical reports in 2024 laid bare the toll of the devastating IPP jail term on his mental health, warning that his “lengthy incarceration” was creating “impermeable barriers” to his recovery.

open image in gallery UN special rapporteur on torture, Dr Alice Jill Edwards, has condemned IPP jail terms ( AFP/Getty )

In an urgent plea to Andy Burnham’s new government and new justice secretary Alex Norris, Pastor White called for them to put right the “huge injustice”.

“The new government has an unprecedented opportunity to fix one of the greatest injustices that no other prime minister has been willing to address,” she added.

“I urge you to prioritise the IPP scandal – a wrongdoing that has contributed to the deaths of almost 100 IPP prisoners.

“My brother, Thomas White, has spent the last nine months as a patient in a forensic psychiatric hospital after years of suffering caused by the torture of the IPP sentence.

“In the coming days, Thomas is due to be returned to prison, as this brief respite from that inhumane system comes to an end. Thomas has now served more than 14 years in custody under an IPP sentence, despite receiving a tariff of just two years.”

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “It is right that IPP sentences were abolished, and as the IPP annual report shows, we have significantly improved support for these offenders.

“They are entitled to aftercare when they leave hospital and have greater access to rehabilitation and mental health support – helping them cope with life outside hospital.

“We are determined to make further progress towards safe and sustainable releases for those on this sentence, but not in any way that undermines public protection.”

News.title: Why India’s ‘cockroach’ protests had such impact – and what could happen next
News.content:

Indians danced, sang songs, and raised victory slogans on the streets on Saturday after prime minister Narendra Modi’s government bowed to the demands of Gen Z protesters seeking the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over a leaked medical entrance exam.

It was a rare setback for Modi but a big win for the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical movement whose young supporters have openly mocked the prime minister and his cabinet colleagues through raps, placards, and graffiti for weeks, demanding accountability for the lapses in how the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Neet) was conducted.

The leak affected some two million students ​in ⁠May, and have been linked to several student suicides.

For a decade, Modi has governed as a strong, decisive figure who admits few ‌mistakes, and his government had long resisted sacking ministers under pressure. Indian farmers ​had to protest for nearly a year before Modi repealed the contentious farm laws in 2021.

The nationwide protests were an almost unthinkable development only weeks earlier in a country whose politics has been almost fully dominated by Modi since he came to power in 2014.

open image in gallery Protesters celebrate after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following nationwide protests as part of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest movement in Mumbai, India, Sunday, 26 July 2026 ( AP )

Earlier this year, there was mounting pressure on the government to sack the federal minister for petroleum and natural gas, Hardeep Singh Puri, over his communication with late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during his time in the United States. Puri, a career diplomat-turned-politician, said he was part of the International Peace Institute, a New York think tank headed by Norwegian diplomat and former cabinet minister Terje Roed-Larsen until 2020, and met Epstein "three or maximum four times" during his time there.

Roed-Larsen has apologised for his connection to Epstein and his wife, Mona Juul, a Norwegian ambassador, stepped down over her links to the US financier and sex offender.

At a time when unpopular governments and ministers either resign or are made to step down in other democracies, Modi’s administration has come to be known for not bowing to public pressure.

Pradhan is only the second minister to resign after public pressure, since Modi came to power. MJ Akbar resigned as junior foreign minister ​in October 2018 to fight allegations of sexual harassment made by more than a dozen women during India's #MeToo movement.

Explaining the importance of the resignation of Pradhan as their primary demand, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das tells The Independent: “It is the very first step to a better, accountable system. The basic level of accountability had to be forced. Heaven and hell had to be moved to force it when it should have been automatic.

open image in gallery Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters celebrate after the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) examination paper leaks, at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, India, 25 July 2026 ( Reuters )

“It was automatic before 2014,” he says, referring to governments prior to that of Modi. Shivraj Patil resigned as the home minister of the country in 2008, taking moral responsibility for the Mumbai terror attack in which 175 people were killed. In 2010, A Raja resigned as minister of communications and IT due to allegations of corruption in the allocation of 2G spectrum.

“But post 2014, the government takes great arrogance in not sacking its minister. So we are restoring that India first and after that we are going to talk about those issues. And what can be implemented immediately, short term, long term and mid term. And later on,” Das says.

Pralhad Joshi took charge of the education ministry on Sunday in addition to the consumer affairs portfolio he holds in Modi’s cabinet, marking an end of the worst political crisis the prime minister faced in his third term as the protests were called off.

Joshi, a five time parliamentarian from Karnataka since 2004, was in his constituency in Dharwad, when he was informed that he had been given charge of the education minister. He took a flight from Hubli to return to Delhi.

The crisis peaked this week when thousands of protesters marched on parliament, with police using tear gas to control them. Young voters form a critical base of Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.

open image in gallery Abhijeet Dipke, founder of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), addresses celebrating supporters following the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, after days of protests demanding he step down over the alleged Neet examination paper leak scandal on 25 July 2026 ( Getty )

Young people, calling themselves "cockroaches", had taken to the streets since late June, forcing a resit which galvanised anger about the lack of prospects for young Indians. Abhijeet Dipke founded the CJP as a mocking response to a pointed comment from India’s top judge, Justice Surya Kant, who likened India’s unemployed youth in a speech to “cockroaches”.

Similar youth-led protest movements brought down governments in neighbouring Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh in ​recent years.

To quell the protests, Modi, 75, posted a rare selfie video in which he said he was pained by the suffering of the youths and promised remedial steps. The video, posted on Thursday on Instagram, where CJP amassed 22 million mainly ⁠Gen Z followers in a matter of days in May, was not enough to satisfy the thousands who had gathered in central Delhi, braved a massive police crackdown days earlier, and then inspired protests across the country.

"The paper leak is a trigger point," political analyst Amitabh Tiwari told Reuters. "It is largely a reflection of the anxiety, nervousness, discontent, frustration and anger among the youth."

open image in gallery Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokespersons Saurav Das (C) and Ashutosh Ranka (R) along with India's Health Minister JP Nadda attend a press conference after their meeting in New Delhi on 25 July 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Indians aged 18 ‌to 40 are estimated to make up about 40 per cent of the population but hold only about 10 per cent of seats in the lower house of parliament, down from more than double that in the 1950s, Tiwari says. The cabinet's average age is more than 60. Though the CJP is not a political party, all opposition parties have tried to cash in on the rare opening they have seen in the protests against Modi, by taking up the cause of ⁠the students.

The first tests of the youth anger could be in elections next year in the most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, in Punjab and Modi's home state of Gujarat. The BJP runs both Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. The bigger risk for Modi could lie in the 2029 national election if the CJP turns itself into a party.

Dipke has said no decision had been made so far on joining electoral politics. Some analysts say young voters have hitherto largely cast ballots along religious or caste lines, benefiting Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). But things may be changing.

The decision to force Pradhan out of the cabinet, however, has not gone down well with the prime minister’s supporters.

“It’s a victory of violence, not of any generation or grievance,” wrote a user, Rahul Roushan.

open image in gallery rmed forces enforce movement restrictions of celebrating demonstrators of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), after days demanding the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan ( Getty )

“For the first time in my life, I can’t hold my head high in front of my leftist friends -- thanks to Modi Ji,” wrote another user.

CJP spokespersons, Ashutosh Ranka and Das, in a joint press conference with federal ministers Jitendra Singh and JP Nadda, announced the withdrawal of the agitation “in good faith”.

Nadda said the government had accepted all demands of the protesters, which included reforms in the exam system, dropping police cases filed against protesters and ‌compensating families of students who died by suicide after the exam paper leaks.

Ranka says: "The bottom line is we have won, your struggle, hard work, and patience have paid off."

open image in gallery A supporter of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) holds a placard as protesters celebrate the resignation of India's education minister Dharmendra Pradhan ( AFP/Getty )

The demonstrations have become one of the most visible signs of public dissent against Modi’s government in recent years, with thousands returning to the streets even after police used tear gas and batons this week to disperse marchers trying to reach parliament.

The protests also reflected growing anger in India over job scarcity and government accountability.

"Young generation is here. This is a win for the constitution,” protester Tluanga Ralte says, walking with a copy of the Indian constitution at the protest site after Pradhan's resignation. "We are not a lazy generation."

An actor – running for his own party and allied with opposition parties – was recently elected chief minister in the prosperous southern state of Tamil Nadu, propelled by his Instagram-first fanbase of Gen Z, the demographic group born from 1997 to 2012.

“This has been a moment of reckoning for PM Modi and it shows how they are completely out of touch with what ‌Gen Z wants," says author Anurag Minus Verma.

open image in gallery Protesters celebrate at Jantar Mantar after reports of the resignation of Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on 25 July 2026 in New Delhi, India ( Getty )

"For years, the BJP's digital political strategy was centred on platforms like X, where much of the political conversation took place. But that conversation has increasingly shifted to Instagram now, particularly among younger users."

The BJP may rule most of India, and calls itself the world's largest ‌political party, but it has managed just 10 million Instagram followers in years, less ⁠than half what the CJP gained in days. The BJP has 23 million followers on X and 18 million on Facebook, though Modi's personal followers on ⁠all three social media platforms are massive, ranging between 60 and 107 million.

"You need a kind of authenticity for Instagram," says columnist Santosh Desai. "Pre-laboured, carefully massaged messages wont work. This medium was created by this generation and has become what it has thanks to this generation. This generation has no reverence."

"From now, a leader who listens is likely to do well," Tiwari says.

News.content:

Tyson Fury won first in seven rounds on Friday night, the next night Anthony Joshua won in two rounds, but that does not tell the story of an extraordinary weekend of fights.

The pair have agreed to fight each other later this year in a massive and long overdue showdown. The harsh truth is that neither victory was impressive.

Fury looked sluggish and Joshua was dropped twice by Kristian Prenga in the opening round before recovering his senses to deliver a stunning knockout.

open image in gallery Joshua climbed off the canvas to avoid a major upset ( PA Archive )

However, there is still no date, no venue and not even confirmation of a country for their long overdue fight. The original signed contracts from two months ago are close to being ripped up; the contracts are only valid if their fight takes place in Britain.

The pair have been linked since they both held versions of the world heavyweight title at the same time in the summer of 2016; it is one of boxing’s longest running sagas, a potentially great fight that is now moving ever closer to collapse.

Joshua was having his first fight since the fatal car crash last December in Lagos; two of Joshua’s closest friends died in the crash - Joshua survived.

He entered the ring in Jeddah looking calm and relaxed, but was sent sprawling by a short right uppercut in the opening 15 seconds. He looked badly hurt, both stunned and dazed. He recovered his feet, was staggered several more times and then touched down again for a second knockdown. The Fury fight looked over. Fury was expected at ringside but never showed. Joshua survived the round - just.

In round two, Prenga never threw a punch, Joshua recovered and knocked out the Albanian with about 20 seconds of the round left. Prenga was out cold, Joshua was ecstatic. It was an impressive comeback.

open image in gallery Joshua leant on his heart - but a showdown with Fury still has hurdles to overcome ( AP )

In Pattaya, Thailand, the night before, Fury finally forced the aging and hulking Polish veteran, Mariusz Wach to quit at the end of seven rounds. It was not vintage Fury, but it was enough on the night in front of a lively crowd at a Muay Thai stadium. The fight was not shown live and will instead be part of a Netflix series about family life in the Fury household.

The consensus, during the past three weeks, was that they would both win their warm-up fights, then Fury would arrive at ringside in Jeddah after a 4,000km journey, Joshua would invite him to the ring, they would face off and announce a date and a venue; the plan seemed to start unravelling when it was clear that New York and Las Vegas were also contenders to stage the fight. Hearn confirmed the contracts - signed by both boxers - were for a fight in Britain only.

“I will fight him anywhere,” insisted Fury. “I just can’t see him in the corner opposite me.”

Fury has long insisted that Joshua will never fight him; Joshua has laughed at the slight. “He’s the one that keeps retiring - I’ve never gone anywhere,” countered Joshua.

open image in gallery Fury was not at Joshua’s fight on Saturday night after competing in front of just 1,500 fans in Thailand ( PA Wire )

Meanwhile, Fury’s business manager, Spencer Brown, did make the arduous journey from ringside in Pattaya to ringside in Jeddah, and was confident the fight will take place. “It’s 100 per cent happening - there will be big news soon,” he insisted.

Nobody expected Joshua to come so close to defeat in a fight that looked like a sensible match, but a mismatch; Prenga came close to ruining the big dreams of the big men.

The fight will be announced in the next week or two, and that will be long enough for everybody involved to look forward, and not back at the two scraps at the very heart of a truly bizarre weekend.

Police believe an attack on a crowd at an LGBTQ+ event in Berlin is an act of Islamist terrorism as the suspect remains on the run.

Germany’s interior minister Alexander Dobrindt said that the suspect rammed people with a car and then attacked the crowd with a blade, which “might have been a machete”.

One person was killed and 29 were injured in the incident at 10pm in the Tiergarten park area of Berlin, where crowds were celebrating the annual Christopher Street Day Parade.

Dobrindt that "everything we are seeing here indicates that we have experienced an Islamist attack".

He said the suspect, named as Abdul B, is on the run and that a large number of officers from Berlin police and the federal police are working to find him.

The 21-year-old is a German citizen of Lebanese background who was known to police. He was previously sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison, which was switched to a non-custodial sentence due to a legal complaint, Dobrindt said.

Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin on Saturday to celebrate at Berlin’s pride parade, known in Germany as Christopher Street Day. It’s one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

Eddie Hearn says the Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua showdown must take place in the UK under the terms of the fight deal signed three months ago.

Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh wants to stage the fight – which is expected to take place in October or November – at a time that would attract a global audience.

Alalshikh would need to gain an exemption to Wembley Stadium’s current curfews to go ahead with his plans for a 2am UK start, and it has now emerged Madison Square Garden in New York is the powerbroker’s preferred choice for the all-British fight.

open image in gallery Wembley Stadium is thought to be the favourite venue to host the encounter ( PA )

But Joshua’s promoter Hearn insists they have signed up for a UK fight only and the contract would have to be renegotiated to move elsewhere.

“There’s a reason we put contracts together,” Hearn said after Joshua’s second-round stoppage of Kristian Prenga kept him on course for a Fury showdown, little more than 24 hours after his British rival had stopped Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

“There’s a reason that AJ employs lawyers. There’s a reason me and him sit down and have endless conversations to make sure that every move is correct.

“We insisted that this fight was in the UK. I know that AJ will sometimes want to be a little bit of a peacekeeper, but the reality is he said to me, ‘I want the fight in the UK. This is a British fight’. I can’t agree more.

“Turki Alalshikh is our partner and has been an unbelievable supporter of Anthony Joshua. It’s not like as if it was Frank Warren (Fury’s promoter) back in the day and we would have made this fight and I’d have said, ‘Spin on it’.

“We would have conversations, but the only way the fight doesn’t take place in England is if Anthony Joshua and myself agree to it because we have a legally binding contract that took a long, long time to negotiate

“Let’s be honest this is a fight for the British public. The MSG, great venue, but this is something that will be remembered across all generations forever.

“There’s nothing I need to do to make the fight. The fight’s signed. The fight’s made. So, we’ll see what the next couple of weeks bring.”

open image in gallery Tyson Fury beat Mariusz Wach in Thailand ( PA )

Joshua believes the legacy of both himself and Fury would be tarnished if their long-awaited meeting is not held in the UK – and the two-time former world champion says Wembley has been agreed to host it.

He said: “When these conversations started, there was no other venue or location that was ever mentioned.

“It was simple. This is the road map. You fight, come back, fight, and then providing you’re victorious, you’ll be fighting Tyson Fury in the UK, basically Wembley.

“I wouldn’t expect it to be at Tottenham (Hotspur Stadium) or the Principality Stadium (Cardiff) respectfully. It’s just got that history when you think of Wembley.

“So I’m not too sure where all this conversation started of different locations, new this that and the other.”

Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv early on Sunday, setting off fires and wounding at least three civilians, while attacks on other parts of Ukraine later killed at least two people, local officials reported.

The strikes come as Ukraine’s successful drone attacks have stalled the Russian army’s advances in an expanded campaign inside Russia that has been causing fuel shortages and piling pressure on Russian leader Vladimir Putin.

In Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine, Kremlin-installed authorities said a Ukrainian drone strike had killed four civilians in the city of Horlivka. According to Ivan Prikhodko, the city’s Russian-appointed mayor, the city had been under fire since the early hours of Sunday.

According to Russia’s defense ministry, Russian forces overnight struck down 133 Ukrainian drones over Russia, the Black Sea and Crimea, the peninsula that Moscow forcibly annexed from Ukraine in 2014.

Russian attacks set fire to tower block near Kyiv center

Blasts rocked Kyiv in the early hours of Sunday, with falling debris sparking a blaze in a tower block near the historic center, according to mayor Vitali Klitschko.

Elsewhere in the capital, falling debris set fire to buildings, cars and car parks, Klitschko added. He said three people had been wounded, with one needing hospital treatment.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned in his evening address on Friday that intelligence assessments indicated that Russia was preparing missiles for a large attack, saying there were indications that this could happen in the next 48 hours.

Russia’s defense ministry claimed on Sunday that its latest attack on Kyiv had struck sites linked to drone production.

Also Sunday, a drone strike on Kharkiv — Ukraine’s second-largest city in the east — killed one person and wounded at least six others, including two children, mayor Igor Terekhov reported.

In the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, a Russian glide bomb killed one man and wounded at least six other people, according to mayor Ivan Fedorov.

Both Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia have been frequent targets for Russian attacks, with Zaporizhzhia — just over 20 kilometers (12.5 miles) from the front line — suffering heavy bombardment in recent months.

Tit-for-tat strikes

On Friday, a major Russian strike near Kyiv killed at least 10 people and wounded around 100 others, part of a cycle of tit-for-tat attacks that dims the potential of reaching a diplomatic end to Russia’s more than 4-year-old invasion of its neighbor.

Meanwhile, Finnish President Alexander Stubb claimed on Sunday that “Ukraine’s position is stronger than ever since the war began".

Following a call with his Ukrainian counterpart — and appearing to allude to Kyiv’s recent drone campaign that has struck major Russian energy sites and sought to choke off military supplies — Stubb wrote on X that “continued support from (Ukraine's) partners is critical to keep up the momentum."

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.title: Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe
News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

Kick-off is at 12.30pm.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: Harry Redknapp warns FA to avoid Pep Guardiola and claims ‘sleepwalking’ England face an Italy-style World Cup nightmare
Sports.content:
HARRY REDKNAPP warns English football is sleepwalking into an Italy-style nightmare — and insists the FA must NOT chase Pep Guardiola.

The former West Ham and Tottenham boss says Thomas Tuchel needs total backing while insisting England’s academy system is quietly collapsing.



With Guardiola turning down the Italy job, Redknapp insists Wembley chiefs should steer away from targeting the former Manchester City manager.

Redknapp said: “Everybody seems to think Pep is some sort of magic wand in football. The bloke is an absolute tactical genius, no doubt about it.



“But you can’t just teleport Pep into the England set-up and suddenly expect guaranteed trophies.

“At club level, Pep’s always had massive money to spend. If he needs a full-back who can step into midfield, he buys a £70million player.

“In international football, there are no chequebooks. You don’t have transfer windows. You get what your country produces, and that’s the end of the story.”

And Redknapp has grave concerns about the future production line of English talent and fears not enough are coming through.

He said: “Italy is a proper warning sign for us. A massive footballing powerhouse missing out on back-to-back World Cups is absolute madness — criminal really.

“Yet, if we aren’t careful, we are sleepwalking straight into the exact same disaster.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“The pipeline of young local talent in Italy has dried up and it’s starting to happen here.”

Having overseen one of the most prolific academy eras in modern English football, Redknapp believes top-flight clubs are drastically undermining their own local production lines.

He said: “Back in my day at West Ham, we had a proper production line coming through — Michael Carrick, Joe Cole, Rio Ferdinand, Frank Lampard, Glen Johnson, Jermain Defoe.

“We had players bursting into the team who lived and breathed the club, knew the culture, and went on to play for the Three Lions.



“It breaks my heart because half these academy boys now don’t even get to watch the first team train. They’re stuck on faraway pitch behind high fences.

“At West Ham, we had the lads sweeping the terraces, staying behind after training, kicking balls against walls and watching the senior pros.

“Now everything is sanitised. You can’t build steel in kids if you insulate them from real senior football.”

To fix the crisis, Redknapp called for strict policy changes within the Premier League, urging that clubs be forced to field homegrown players rather than buying foreign squad options.



Redknapp said: “There should be rules in place where Premier League clubs have to field a set number of English players. That’s how you protect our future.

“Right now, top clubs just go abroad to buy ready-made players, and our young homegrown lads get blocked at every turn.”

Maintaining his traditionalist view on international management, Redknapp argued that national teams should strictly employ managers from their own country.

He said: “In an ideal world, an English national team should be led by an English manager.

“The Spain manager is Spanish. The France manager is French. The Argentina manager was Argentinian who used to play for West Ham!



“We’ve got brilliant managers like Eddie Howe who know our culture.

“Plus top former players like Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard who have cut their teeth in management.

“But it’s clear the only way English managers usually get Premier League jobs is if they get promoted from the Championship.



“If we don’t trust and back our own coaches, what message are we sending to the next generation?”

Redknapp urged the nation to get behind the current boss Tuchel for the task ahead while fixing the long-term system.

The former manager said: “Don’t get me wrong, we’ve actually got a fantastic squad of players right now who are more than good enough to go and win a major trophy.

“So let’s forget about chasing Pep. Let’s give Tuchel our full backing for the job ahead.

“And let’s sort out our youth development before we end up like the Italians, watching the World Cup from the sofa at home.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel accused of single-handedly ‘f***ing up’ World Cup campaign by England star’s former boss
Sports.content:
MANAGERIAL legend Barry Fry is still fuming that Thomas Tuchel “f***ed up” England’s World Cup bid by snubbing Ivan Toney.

Fry launched Toney’s career at Peterborough before selling him on to Brentford six years ago.



Posh’s Director of Football was delighted when Tuchel called his former star player up for his World Cup squad.

The appointment may have stunned most pundits but Fry knew exactly what an asset Toney could be for his country.



But Tuchel ignored Toney, who now plays for Al-Ahli Saudi FC, for most of the campaign until the Three Lions had lost the chance to win another star on their shirts.

The German gave the striker just two minutes action in the heart-breaking semi-final defeat to Argentina before starting him in the exciting third-place play-off against France.



Yet the damage had already been done in Fry’s eyes after seeing the Three Lions throw away another golden chance of glory.

“We f***ed it up and there’s only one man to blame,” slammed Fry, 81, who rescued the career of Newcastle reject Toney.

“Ivan was the only striker in the squad who was acclimatised to play in those conditions in the US and Mexico.

“He has played his football in the heat of Saudi Arabia and has been top scorer for two seasons out there – but still he wasn’t used.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I was delighted when he was called up because I thought it was a smart move because I didn’t think Harry Kane could last 90 minutes in every game.

“But Harry did better than I thought he would do but looked exhausted trying to defend in the second half against Argentina-but Toney was left on the bench until near the end of stoppage time.”

Fry loved having Toney leading his Peterborough line because the player was a major asset at both ends of the field.

Fry said: “Not only was he an excellent forward for us but he was my best defender as well defending set-pieces.



“If he had come on against Argentina he would have upset their defenders and caused mayhem because he’s a f***ing nuisance.

“He would have got one or two of them booked and maybe red-carded because that’s what he does.

“But I felt for him because he didn’t get the chance to show what he can do, especially when England needed someone like him to hold the ball upfront.

“Sitting back and allowing Argentina to have the ball was only going to end one way and Tuchel must take the blame.”



The German, who blamed the players’ DNA for the defeat, has escaped the FA bullet and will lead the Three Lions into Euro 2028 on these shores.

By then England’s record-breaking striker Kane will be approaching 34 while Toney will be two years younger.

Fry added: “They had to keep Tuchel because they gave him a new contract before the tournament started-and I hope he gives Ivan another chance.”

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel takes in World Cup disappointment with London bike ride
Sports.content:
ENGLAND coach Thomas Tuchel gets a grip on his World Cup ­disappointment — by taking a ride on an electric hire bike.

The 52-year-old Three Lions boss looked in need of a pick-me-up as he went on a coffee run in ­Notting Hill, West London.



He bought himself a drink and handed another to a homeless woman.

A week earlier, he guided England to a 6-4 win over France to seal third place, our best World Cup finish since 1966.



But it came after an agonising 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

England had been leading until the 85th minute.

Tuchel came in for heavy criticism due to the substitutions he made while trying to protect England’s 1-0 lead.

The German coach then said England lacked the ‘DNA’ to control possession.



Midfielder Jude ­Bellingham, meanwhile, chilled at Disneyland, California, with his ­girlfriend Ashlyn Castro.

And his teammate Declan Rice was at Disney in Florida with his nephew.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reunites with ex-boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in Norway before praising Man Utd’s academy stars
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK praised Manchester United’s academy gems for playing with swagger in the club’s 5-0 preseason win over Rosenborg.

Carrick again started with a strong side in Trondheim, but brought on two youngsters at the break in full backs Harry Amass and Jaydan Kamason.



Kamason produced two brilliantly worked assists, while Amass scored and played a fake one-two with Joshua Zirkzee to set up the Dutchman’s stunner.

Eight more youngsters arrived on the hour mark, with Jacob Devaney, on at centre-back, instantly finding the net before Ethan Williams completed the riot.



While it is still early days in pre-season, the most of the younger players have covered themselves in glory against Wrexham in Helsinki, and a limited Rosenborg side in Trondheim.

Carrick told MUTV in Norway: “That’s the best way to be as a footballer, when you’re in that zone and you’re confident, that’s my job to try and get the players in that frame of mind.

“The younger players, when you see them expressing themselves and being themselves and keep pushing themselves to be better.

“Some of the play in the second half was really, really good and I was delighted to see that from them.

“They’ve all got potential in different ways, and you want them to fulfil it and keep pushing themselves, and they certainly did that.”

Carrick met up with his former boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer before the match on Friday.

The pair were both considered to take over from Ruben Amorim when the Portuguese was sacked in January.

Carrick did most of the coaching during Solskjaer’s three years in charge and that played a major part in the Geordie getting the nod over the Norwegian.

The pair have remained close friends and keep in touch, and Solskjaer’s family home in Kristiansund is a three hour drive from Trondheim.

Carrick worked under Solskjaer during United’s preseason friendly in Oslo against Kristiansund BK in July 2019.

Sports.title: New PM Andy Burnham actively considering letting football fans drink in stands again
Sports.content:
ANDY Burnham’s Government is actively considering letting football fans drink in the stands again.

Officials are considering whether to review restrictions which stop people consuming alcohol in view of the pitch.



The ban was introduced in 1985 to stop football hooligans fighting.

Other sports like rugby were not affected.



A government spokesperson said: “We are considering the case being made by some clubs and supporter groups for reviewing the current restrictions on alcohol consumption at football matches.

“The safety of football fans remains our priority, and any future consideration of changes would need to be evidence-led and informed by the views of policing and safety authorities, as well as clubs, supporters and other partners across the football sector.”

It comes just weeks after the new Prime Minister said it was “wrong” that spectators could not enjoy a pint during matches.

Everton fan Mr Burnham made the comments while watching a rugby league match at the club’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.



In a social media clip while holding a pint, he said: “How come these lads can do that in my seat here when we can’t do that at an Everton home game?

“There’s something wrong there, we need to take a look at that.”

This week the new Prime Minister announced that pubs, social clubs and live music venues will be given a 20 per cent cut to business rates from April.

Landlords welcomed the change but called on the Labour leader to go further by slashing VAT on boozers too.

The new Prime Minister insisted he was ready to protect “working-class culture” – in a win for The Sun’s Save Our Sups campaign.



More than 30,000 venues will save an estimated £1,100 each in the next financial year from the business rates cut.

Sports.title: Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video
Sports.content:
Wolves release statement after player involved in viral England under-16 fight video

Footage of two England under-16 players fighting inside a hotel room as their team-mates watched emerged on social media this week, and now Wolves have confirmed that one of their academy prospects was involved

View Image The two England players were filmed fighting

Wolves have issued a statement confirming that a member of their academy was one of the players filmed fighting a team-mate during an England under-16 camp in Turkey last year. Footage emerged on social media this week showing the pair scrapping in a hotel room, as other players watched on.

‌



Several of their team-mates were filming the incident and could be heard encouraging them. The FA issued a statement saying that the fight was caused by an 'internal matter' and was 'quickly resolved'.

‌



Championship club Wolves have now addressed the viral video in a statement published on their website, saying that the footage only captures part of a 'broader sequence of events'. It read: "Wolves are aware of footage from a previous England youth camp involving one the club's academy players which has recently resurfaced on social media.

‌



"The club is satisfied that the widely shared footage captures only part of a much broader sequence of events and does not reflect the full circumstances surrounding the incident, during which the young player had been subjected to repeated behaviour that caused him significant distress.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Trent Alexander-Arnold's pick for England manager has just taken different job READ MORE :

"Wolves staff are disappointed by those continuing to share the footage in question and condemn, in the strongest possible terms, those who have sought to identify, threaten and abuse the young person involved. Instances of extreme abuse and threats have already been shared with police."

‌



A one-minute clip of the fight showed a boy wearing official England training gear grab a phone from another boy who was lying on the bed of a hotel room. The two can be seen grappling over the phone before punches and kicks were thrown.

The boy who tried to take the phone then attempts to put the other in a headlock. He subsequently dragged him around the room before throwing him on the floor.

In the statement, Wolves academy director Jonathan Hunter-Barrett added: "Whilst the academy does not condone violence under any circumstances, it is important to recognise that this footage captures only the final moments of a much longer sequence of events. It does not reflect the repeated behaviour this young player had been subjected to, the significant distress he had experienced beforehand, or the circumstances that led to the incident.

‌



"Those of us who know this young man understand that the footage is not an accurate reflection of either his character or the circumstances he found himself in. He is respectful, humble and has consistently demonstrated the standards and values we expect from our academy players, earning the respect of both staff and teammates through the way he conducts himself every day.

Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months READ MORE :

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

"Like all young people, Academy players learn and develop through both positive and difficult experiences. We are incredibly proud of the person he is today, and of the way he has responded to this distressing incident and the subsequent attention it has received, both when the footage first emerged in 2025 and again in recent days.

"This has been an extremely difficult period for him and his family. Our priority is their welfare, and we will continue to provide them with the care and support they need.

‌



"We would also encourage people to consider the impact of sharing and commenting on footage involving minors and young people. Behind every video is a person and a family, and their wellbeing should always be at the forefront of our minds.

"As a club, we do not tolerate bullying, intimidation or abuse in any form. Supporting and protecting the welfare of our young people will always be our priority, and our commitment is to continue supporting young players in their development, both as footballers and, more importantly, as people."

Sports.title: Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen
Sports.content:
Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen

Vinicius Jr has been linked with a sensational move to the Premier League to join Arsenal

View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Spanish media have given their say on the possibility of Vinicius Jr joining Arsenal. The Real Madrid winger is wanted by the Gunners but talks between the clubs have yet to begin.

‌



The 26-year-old is in the final 12 months of his contract and if Real can't secure an extension, they could be open to selling in order to avoid losing him for free next summer. A number of Spanish newspapers have weighed in on whether the transfer could actually happen.

‌



Sport claims that Real president Florentino Perez has set a non-negotiable fee of £136million (€160m). The media outlet understands that the club will not bat an eyelid at a figure below this for Vini's signature.

‌



Real are considering this fee to be an initial purchase with a number of add-ons, including performance bonuses and trophies won. Should Arsenal meet these demands, Sport sees no reason as to how the deal couldn't go through.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update READ MORE :

Arsenal have trump card to beat Man Utd in £40m Ollie Watkins transfer race READ MORE :

Marca aren't as confident that the transfer will happen though. The Spanish newspaper states that Vini is demanding at least £25m (€30m) per season to bring his salary close to Kylian Mbappe's.

They believe the contract extension negotiations are entering a "delicate phase" and if these conditions aren't met, it is unclear what the future holds for the winger. Cadena SER believes that the arrival of Yan Diomande could be the end of Vini in Spain.

View 2 Images Vini Jr wants a similar salary to Kylian Mbappe (Image: Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The media outlet claims that Real's pursuit of the Ivory Coast international showcases the club's movement into a new era. The La Liga giants saw a £85.4m bid rejected by RB Leipzig and are now submitting an improved offer, believing that a deal can be done.

The pair would be competing for the left wing spot and Real's growing interest in Diomande is a hint to the media that Vini Jr is on his way out. They did admit that there is a world where both wingers remain in Spain but Vini's recent links to Arsenal could mean the 19-year-old is his replacement under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical done as signing is agreed hours after Vinicius Jr transfer update

Arsenal want Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior and are exploring a move for the Brazil international, but have already agreed to sign another player this summer

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are adding another player to their academy (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Cardiff City's youngest-ever player, Axel Donczew, is set to sign for Arsenal next week.

‌



The Gunners have agreed a deal for the Wales under-19 international, who Fabrizio Romano claims has already had a medical.

‌



Donczew, 16, debuted for the Bluebirds as a second-half substitute during their EFL Trophy match against Newport County in October, aged 15 years and 234 days. He broke a record that his team-mate Rob Tankiewicz set barely an hour earlier by starting the group stage game.

‌



Aaron Ramsey had previously held the record for 18 years. He was also the last player Arsenal signed from Cardiff.

The Gunners spent £7million on a 17-year-old Ramsey in 2018. That move came after the midfielder made 22 appearances across all competitions for Cardiff, whereas Donczew has played just twice.

The Telegraph initially reported that the Gunners were keen on the teenager, who is expected to join their academy.

‌



News of the deal surfaced less than 24 hours after Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior emerged. Real Madrid's winger would likely cost a record-breaking fee for the Gunners to sign, but they are believed to be exploring the possibility.

Jose Mourinho is reportedly reluctant to lose the Brazilian, but his lack of a new contract at the Bernabeu means Real could cash in this summer.

In terms of Donczew, he has been missing from Cardiff City's pre-season activities this summer following interest from Premier League sides. Fulham had previously expressed interest in the right-footed left winger, who can also play centrally as an attacking midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City's former Elite Development Sqyad head coach Brian Barry-Murphy believes Axel Donczew is a brilliant player (Image: Ryan Hiscott, Getty Images)

Donczew last played for Cardiff in December, making another substitute appearance during an EFL Trophy round of 32 tie against Wimbledon. A fortnight later, Donczew was included in the matchday squad for their EFL Cup quarter-final against Chelsea, but did not feature.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy said late last year: "I think if they're good enough, and he clearly is, then they're old enough for us with Axel. The former Manchester City youth coach hailed Donczew as a "brilliant player".

‌



He has already earned recognition as a Wales under-19 international. Donczew has represented his national side since the under-15s.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The youngster has racking up 11 appearances across various age groups, and also holds eligibility to feature for Poland. Wales senior side head coach Craig Bellamy, however, is said to be an admirer of the youngster.

‌



Under-21s coach Darren Purse told WalesOnline: "I think Axel came into fruition because I think Craig Bellamy really liked him as an Under-16 playing for Wales. I think that came through him and the gaffer's (Barry-Murphy) conversations."

CAA (Creative Artists Agency) Stellar represents Donczew. The prominent agency's lengthy list of clients also notably includes two current Arsenal academy players: Angelinou Pedro and Theo Julienne.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet's Liverpool absence explained as summer signing left OUT of pre-season squad

Liverpool saw off Sunderland in a pre-season friendly on Saturday but they did so without Jeremy Jacquet as the summer signing was left out of the squad

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet was left out of Liverpool's squad at the weekend

Andoni Iraola admits Jeremy Jacquet's long-term injury led to him being left out of Liverpool's squad on Saturday with the Reds prepared to "take it easy with him".

‌



The French defender was signed in January for £55million from Rennes, but allowed to play out the season with the Ligue 1 club. He's since made the move to Anfield but did so off the back of a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

‌



The 21-year-old was forced to miss the final few months of last season after picking up a shoulder injury. Given that he have surgery on the issue, his last game came all the way back on February 7.

‌



As a result Liverpool are taking a cautious approach to bringing him back into the fold and he was left out of the team that beat Sunderland 4-2 in Nashville. Iraola explained to LFCTV: “With Jeremy, we decided to take it easy with him."

“He has been a lot of months without playing with a shoulder injury. So, I think we are going to take it easy with him. He will play probably the last game of this US tour and he will have time to have minutes. It's true that we were kind of happy but we've lost one now.”

Iraola was referring to the injury sustained by Joe Gomez, who failed to complete ten minutes during Liverpool's clash on Saturday. There is no diagnosis on his injury but the defender has been plagued by injuries for years and could further test the team's backline depth.

‌



"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe," said Iraola. "We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away."

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet's move to Liverpool was confirmed this summer

Liverpool have seen Ibrahima Konate depart for Real Madrid after his contract expired whilst Giovanni Leoni is still getting back to 100 percent after rupturing his ACL last September. Virgil van Dijk has just turned 35 and will see his contract expire in the summer.

Article continues below

Jacquet is highly rated and was tipped to move to Chelsea, who had chased him throughout January, before Liverpool swooped in to complete a deal. He's relatively inexperienced but is likely to play a big role with Liverpool's resources already being tested in pre-season.
