Sports.title: Sunderland star reveals tactical fix Andoni Iraola has made to Liverpool after one game
Sports.content:
Sunderland star reveals tactical fix Andoni Iraola has made to Liverpool after one game

Liverpool are already proving to be a different beast after one pre-season game under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds played their first game under their new boss in a 4-2 victory over Premier League rivals Sunderland on their tour of the USA.



2 Iraola has already been hard at work putting his stamp on the squad Credit: Getty

And Black Cats defender Dan Ballard has admitted the Reds are a different prospect to facing Arne Slot's side last season.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw at Anfield last December, with a late Nordi Mukiele own-goal rescuing a point for the home side.

Liverpool then became the first team to win away at the Stadium of Light in the Premier League in February after a Virgil van Dijk second-half header edged a 1-0 win.



However, the margin of victory was far greater in the US, with goals from Kieran Morrison, Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas seeing the Reds triumph 4-2.

While the match was only a friendly, Sunderland's Ballard revealed he has already felt the differences between Iraola's and Slot's football.



What has changed for Liverpool?

"I think there's a lot of differences," The 26-year-old told reporters post-match.

"The new gaffer sets the team up in the press very different and he's very intense the way he wants his teams to play.



"We did a lot of work looking at Bournemouth's team last year, and they're very aggressive in the press.

"They play very vertically, and they go straight for goal, which is a little bit different to Slot's team, a little bit more possession-based.

"They gave us a little bit more time on the ball last year, which we were quite surprised at playing Liverpool, knowing them throughout the years."

Former Liverpool talisman Mohamed Salah had previously hinted at the players not being enamoured with Slot's tactics last season.



The Egyptian, who is now a free agent after leaving the club, issued a written statement on social media, appearing to take aim at Slot.

Salah insisted the club should return to their 'heavy metal tactics', a reference to Jurgen Klopp's style of play in his early Anfield years.

Liverpool seemingly agreed by announcing their decision to sack Slot weeks later after concluding that 'the team’s trajectory is best addressed through a change of direction.'

Iraola's front-footed football that proved popular at Bournemouth was quickly identified for the next era at Anfield.



Speaking after his first unofficial win as Liverpool boss, the Spaniard said: "It was difficult to put rhythm into the game.

2 Iraola claimed Liverpool have given themselves a 'good starting point' after beating Sunderland Credit: AFP

"I think both teams were lacking some freshness and it was also humid. The pitch was quite slow.

"We had some good spells on the ball. I think we lacked a little bit of intensity. You can feel the timing is still not there.



"We have to work a lot more, but it's a starting point."

On his team going after the game to try to win in the second half, Iraola added: "It was a matter of using the game to push ourselves and to go back to the rhythm that we should have.

"You play 45, 60 [or] whatever the minutes you play, use them properly.

"It doesn't matter the result, but keep pushing, don't relax, get used to not playing too comfortable. We still have a lot of things to improve."

Sports.title: Arsenal set to step up Bruno Guimaraes transfer chase in bid to end Newcastle standoff
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to step up Bruno Guimaraes transfer chase in bid to end Newcastle standoff

Arsenal are set to accelerate talks for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes in the next week, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners have made the Magpies captain a priority signing and have hope of striking an agreement before the month is out.



4 Newcastle skipper Guimaraes could be on his way out of St James' Park this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Newcastle insist formal talks are yet to begin, but talkSPORT understands verbal discussions are ongoing with Newcastle's senior leadership now directly involved.

Arsenal to accelerate talks for Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal are prepared to pay north of £70million, while Guimaraes has already agreed broad terms, as talkSPORT revealed earlier this month.

Newcastle have been left frustrated over speculation regarding Guimaraes' future, and insiders are surprised by Arsenal's lack of a formal bid to date.



Yet Arsenal sources have told talkSPORT three verbal offers have already been placed.

The clubs clearly disagree on what constitutes a bid, which may in part be down to semantics and also the use of intermediaries.



Newcastle can ill afford to lose their captain this summer, having already seen Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon depart.

Star winger Gordon joined Barcelona in a £70m deal, while Tonali moved to Tottenham for a total package worth around £100m.



The departure of Guimaraes would see Newcastle lose two of last season's midfield three, though they have strengthened in that area having brought in Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba from Ajax and Monaco respectively.

Guimaraes still has two years left on his contract, and the Magpies are under no pressure to sell after losing two of their key players already.

4 Arsenal are working hard on their title defence, and want to add Guimaraes to their midfield Credit: Getty

4 The Brazilian helped end a 70-year wait for a major trophy at Newcastle with League Cup glory last year Credit: Getty



Howe will this play out?

With Arsenal stepping up their pursuit of Guimaraes, Newcastle boss Eddie Howe admitted on Saturday he does not know what the future holds for his skipper.

The Magpies played out a 1-1 draw away at Gateshead, and after the match, Howe was asked about his captain.

He said: “I’ve spoken to Bruno before, during and after the World Cup. We have had some really good conversations. He’s just a fantastic person.

“I don’t know what’s going to happen with his future; that’s for other people to speculate about. There’s conversations I’m not part of.



"I don’t think it’s fair to compare (to Isak last summer). You’ve got to look at it in its own right.

“He’s captain of our club and been an unbelievable player, through the whole time we have worked together.

4 Howe is not sure if his captain will stay at the club beyond the summer Credit: Getty

"I speak on behalf of everyone at the club; we absolutely love him, and of course everyone would love him to stay.



“He’s due back on the 31st [of July], and there’s nothing to say he won’t be back.”

talkSPORT understands Newcastle also want quick clarity over Guimaraes' future.

Sources are reticent to compare the situation to the Alexander Isak saga given Newcastle believe Guimaraes won't refuse to participate in pre-season or play for Newcastle again.

He remains a popular member of the dressing room, and Newcastle have received no indication Guimaraes will act anything other than professionally.



However, Newcastle don't want speculation to drag on all summer, while those close to Guimaraes have told talkSPORT he would prefer his future resolved sooner rather than later as well.

The Brazilian is still on a break following the World Cup. Newcastle would be prepared to offer Guimaraes a new deal if he remains.

Newcastle sources also indicate a £70m bid would be rejected, but talkSPORT understands Arsenal are prepared to go higher than this reported number.

Sports.title: Argentina handed automatic World Cup 2030 spot as Gianni Infantino letter leaks
Sports.content:
Argentina will qualify automatically for the 2030 World Cup – despite hosting just one game at the tournament.

The 2030 World Cup, the competition's centenary edition, is being co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco – with three special anniversary games in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.

3 Argentina reached a second successive World Cup final but were unable to defend their crown Credit: Getty

Uruguay won the inaugural 1930 World Cup, beating Argentina in the final.

Paraguay, meanwhile, is home to the headquarters of South American governing body CONMEBOL, the oldest of the six continental football federations.

Why will Argentina qualify for the 2030 World Cup?

As such, a match is set to be held in each of the three countries' capitals, Montevideo, Buenos Aires and Asuncion.

And, in an unprecedented move, FIFA have confirmed all six host nations will be given an automatic spot at the finals.

The fallout from Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain last weekend continues.

What happened after the 2026 World Cup final?

There were shocking scenes at full-time as scuffles broke out between Argentina players and staff and the victorious Spain team.

Before that, a number of Argentina players celebrated their semi-final win over England by displaying a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son argentinas' ('The Falklands are Argentine'), which the UK government urged FIFA to investigate.

And more controversy has been sparked by FIFA president Gianni Infantino's letter of congratulations to the Argentine FA leaking.

"Dear Mr. President, Yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026, after an exciting final against Spain,’ the Daily Mail report Infantino saying.

"I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer.

3 Messi had to settle for a silver medal this time round but Argentina still got a letter from FIFA president Infantino Credit: Getty

"The FIFA World Cup 2026 will remain in memory as an unforgettable celebration of football, marked by spectacular matches, the irruption of new promises, the presence of the great figures of the sport and the extraordinary atmosphere lived in stadiums full of fans.

"The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world.

"Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

"These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football.

"I wish you, dear Mr. President, all the best for the next competitions and I hope to see you again very soon. With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino."

All three medal-winning nations – including bronze winners England – receive a letter from Infantino, but his message to Argentina was bound to provoke a strong reaction after FIFA opened an investigation into the Albiceleste's behaviour at the end of the final.

3 Argentina's Leandro Paredes (No5) was among those who lashed out after losing the 2026 World Cup final Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, over 20 million people signed a petition calling for Argentina to be permanently banned from the World Cup.

Infuriated football fans had accused FIFA of showing favouritism towards the three-time world champions – who won their most recent title in 2022 – and captain Lionel Messi, allegations FIFA's chief refereeing officer Pierluigi Collina vehemently denied.

The petition has since been closed.

What will the 2030 World Cup look like?

The 2026 World Cup was the biggest edition of the competition yet, increased in size from 32 teams to 48.

But the 2030 tournament looks set to be even bigger and feature 64 teams.

CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez has all but confirmed as much, posting on X: "In 2030, the World Cup comes to Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay, a great opportunity for football to celebrate the World Cup Centenary with a 64-team tournament."

Dominguez's post came as former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, currently FIFA's chief of global football development, lauded the expanded 2026 World Cup as "a great success".

"There were question marks about, 'but the countries were not good enough', and they were given the answer. Not only have they shown that they were good enough, but they gave some great games and entertainment," he said.

Sports.title: 2034 World Cup final venue to be one of world’s biggest arenas as host nation pours $26bn into project
Sports.content:
The 2034 World Cup is part of an unprecedented investment program that will transform Saudi Arabia.

2034 World Cup final venue to be one of world’s biggest arenas as host nation pours $26bn into project

Saudi Arabia is pulling out all the stops for the 2034 World Cup.

Much like Qatar in 2022, a massive nationwide building program will create the necessary infrastructure from the ground up.

4 King Salman Stadium is known as the ‘germinating seed’ Credit: Populous

The tournament will be held across 15 stadiums, with eight being built from scratch, three already in progress and four current venues being renovated.

King Salman International Stadium will be the pick of the bunch.

With around 92,000 seats, it will be one of the world's biggest football stadiums, albeit considerably smaller than the one Morocco hopes will host the 2030 final.

The project is being built north of Riyadh City with an estimated completion date of 2029.

A royal box will hold 150 guests, with 120 hospitality suites, three hundred VIP seats, and two thousand premium spaces to allow FIFA to host plenty of dignitaries -- and likely streamers.

Sustainable cooling systems will work on the seats and the ground, with screens and indoor gardens helping to keep it cool.

The tournament will likely take place in winter -- and may even be in 2035 -- when temperatures should be comfortable enough for fans to enjoy a rooftop walking path overlooking King Abdulaziz Park.

Saudi Arabia is keen to ensure the legacy of the tournament benefits future generations and King Salman International Stadium will be surrounded by training pitches, fan zones, an Olympic swimming pool and athletics track, as well as facilities for racket sports and basketball.

A sports trail over five miles long will connect the stadium and nearby park.

All of this comes at a price.

4 Fans will be able to walk on the roof Credit: Populous

4 92,000 fans will be kept out of the harsh sun Credit: Populous

Along with the stadiums, the country needed to build 65,000 new hotel rooms to meet FIFA's expectations.

SNB Capital estimated the total cost of hosting the tournament at $26 billion.

The hope is that the World Cup will be the culmination of an ambitious repositioning that began in 2019 when the Kingdom's Public Investment Fund launched a project called Vision 2030, hoping to turn it into a sport and entertainment hub.

By 2030, the sector is expected to provide $16.5 billion in benefits, accounting for 1.5 per cent of the national GDP, and create 100,000 jobs.

Saudi citizens have seen participation rates in physical activities increase dramatically with 50 per cent of the population now exercising regularly, up from 13 per cent in 2015.

Female participation has also increased by 400 per cent since 2015.

4 Designs show a thriving mixed-use development Credit: Populous

Esports and digital gaming form another prong of the project with $38 billion allocated.

The Kingdom has already hosted the Esports World Cup.

Can 2034 World Cup be moved?

A report from American outlet Politico has revealed an 'unprecedented scheduling dilemma.'

The Qatar World Cup was held from November 20 to December 18, which will clash with Ramadan in 2034.

Earlier in the year, the Winter Olympics is slated for January and February and March sees around two million pilgrims head to Mecca for Hajj.

Politico suggests that between Christmas 2034 and Hajj -- set for mid-February in 2035 -- could be the most logical window, which could be too short to fit in an expanded tournament with FIFA keen on 48 or even 64 teams.

Sports.title: Liverpool star who only joined last summer among three players fighting for immediate future
Sports.content:
Liverpool star who only joined last summer among three players fighting for immediate future

Liverpool's new era under Andoni Iraola unofficially gets under way this weekend with the club's first pre-season game.

The ex-Bournemouth head coach has been eager to dish out fresh starts for several players, who were fringe players in the old regime.



7 Iraola has a completely different project at Liverpool than he did at Bournemouth Credit: Getty

What's happened at Liverpool?

The Reds have been cleaning house following Arne Slot's sacking last month, with a host of background staff also relieved of their duties.

Michael Edwards has stepped down as Fenway Sports Group's (FSG) CEO of football, while sporting director Richard Hughes has been linked with a move to Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal.

Meanwhile, a consortium backed by the Mittal family are also in talks to buy a minority stake in Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.



On the pitch, Iraola has taken charge of a Liverpool team in transition, with Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, and Ibrahima Konate all departing at the end of last season.

The Spaniard has brought Tommy Elphick from Bournemouth as a first-team coach, but transfer activity remains thin on the ground.



Jeremy Jacquet has officially arrived from Rennes after a deal for the 21-year-old was agreed on deadline day of the winter window.

During the World Cup, Liverpool then signed Spain's Victor Munoz, having successfully hijacked Newcastle's move for the winger.



However, Iraola's pre-season squad - made even thinner by stars on an extended break following their international exploits - has provided an opportunity for fringe players to stake their claims.

Here, talkSPORT.com runs through three players who have the most to prove to their new boss that they should be in next season's plans.

7 Szoboszlai won't have to worry after underlining his importance to Liverpool's project with his new contract Credit: Getty

Trey Nyoni: 'Pre-season tour is an opportunity'

The 19-year-old understandably realises that the Reds' pre-season tour of the USA is an ideal opportunity to prove his qualities to Iraola.



He told Liverpoolfc.com: “It’s exciting times ahead. It’s been good to be back and to see everyone again, and I’m ready to go.

“There are still a few players away [due to the World Cup] so obviously there’s an opportunity to play [in the USA] and just show what I can do in that sense.

“But I’ll just go out there and just enjoy it and just try to do my best.”

Nyoni was one of two Liverpool starlets tipped for a breakout season in 2025/26, with the other living up to the billing in Rio Ngumoha.



7 Nyoni wasn't afforded the opportunities Ngumoha was to steal the spotlight Credit: Getty

He impressed in Arne Slot's first pre-season in 2024, but made just five senior outings, with his fortunes unchanged last campaign.

The England U19 international only managed six Premier League appearances last season - which added up to a combined 21 minutes.

Now, with Curtis Jones looking increasingly likely to stay amid interest from Inter, a pathway to a midfield spot at Liverpool remains blocked.



For Nyoni, a move to Swansea City has been mooted, with former Anfield coach Vitor Matos in charge of the Championship outfit.

The ex-Leicester City academy talent will have a major opportunity in the USA to convince Iraola his immediate future is at Liverpool.

7 Nyoni made 14 senior appearances across all competitions last season

Elliott 'will have a chance during pre-season'

This time last year, Harvey Elliott had the world at his feet after his starring role in the Young Lions' defence of their U21 Euro title.



The 23-year-old was named the player of the tournament after scoring five goals for Lee Carsley's side - which was second only to Newcastle's record signing, Nick Woltemade.

His standout success escalated his ambition to leave boyhood club Liverpool, having made just six starts in the 2024/25 season.

He ultimately joined Aston Villa on deadline day on an initial loan with a £35million obligation to buy once he made 10 league appearances.

Unfortunately for Elliott, Unai Emery quickly stated publicly that his side had no interest in signing him from Liverpool permanently.



7 Elliott effectively lost a year of his career after being exiled at Villa Credit: Getty

Villa's stance meant the Fulham academy talent was either excluded from most matchday squads or left languishing on the bench.

Elliott played just 13 Premier League minutes from the end of September until returning to Liverpool for pre-season this summer.

The attacker only has one-year remaining on his Anfield contract, but new boss Iraola has claimed he will receive a genuine chance during pre-season rather than being forced straight back out the door.



“Harvey is here with us. He has come [in early] also,” Iraola told reporters in his first press conference earlier this month.

“I’ve seen him with this eagerness to show himself, to get himself ready again. He will have a chance during the pre-season; we will need him.

“It’s a good sign that he came a week earlier; he’s been training with the under-21s, and I hope we can see him in a good place.

“I think Harvey, last season, had to be very difficult for him, because it was a strange situation where basically they couldn’t even put him in to play.



“I think he uses what he has experienced, the bad situation, to make him even more eager to be a Liverpool player, yes.”

7 Elliott returned early to pre-season and began preparatory work with Liverpool's U21 squad Credit: Getty

Frimponged

Jeremie Frimpong was the first arrival of the Reds' record-breaking £416m summer spend 12 months ago.

The Netherlands international had the best opportunity to hit the ground running as the replacement for Trent Alexander-Arnold.



He scored in the Community Shield loss to Crystal Palace in August, but then suffered an injury on his Premier League debut.

That proved a sign of things to come, as Frimpong tweaked his hamstring in a 5-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt in mid-September.

His second injury ensured that the Dutchman didn't start another Premier League game until after Christmas.

7 Frimpong had an injury-plagued first season as a Liverpool player Credit: Getty



A third hamstring setback in January only compounded his issues, and Frimpong ultimately missed out on a place in the World Cup.

In total, the former Bayer Leverkusen man started just 12 Premier League games, of which only seven were at right-back.

Conor Bradley remains a long-term absentee after suffering serious bone and ligament damage in his knee in January, with midfielders Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai forced to deputise in the position.

Iraola has already confirmed that the Reds are looking to find a solution at right-back, which could spell bad news for Frimpong.



"So with the centre-back and the right-back situations in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, really thin right now, and it is a solution we are trying to find, yes," he said.

This pre-season will be a vital opportunity for Frimpong to see if he can convince Iraola that an understudy, not a replacement, is needed.

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua fights back tears as he dedicates dramatic victory over Kristian Prenga to two best friends killed in car crash as he recovers from TWO knockdowns to win on return
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua fights back tears as he dedicates dramatic victory over Kristian Prenga to two best friends killed in car crash as he recovers from TWO knockdowns to win on return

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua knows better than anyone how quickly heavyweight boxing can tear up the script. And for a moment on Saturday night in Jeddah, it looked as though another shock was unfolding as the British heavyweight was dropped twice and wrestled to the canvas in a chaotic opening round.

But Joshua dug deep, weathered the storm and, after finding another gear in the second, produced a devastating combination that flattened Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga, leaving the 35-year-old sprawled on his back and bringing a dramatic end to a fight that had threatened to derail his comeback before it had even begun.

Although, when AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary.

For the first time since returning to the ring, the grief that he had worked so hard to suppress finally appeared.

The former two-time heavyweight world champion appeared, perhaps for the first time in public, to let the emotions he had buried since Latif 'Latz' Ayodele and Sina Ghami's tragic deaths in a car crash in Nigeria last December finally surface.

Joshua admitted before the fight that he had spent months suppressing the pain of losing the two men - Latz, his strength coach, and Sina, his personal trainer - insisting he did not want to make their deaths about himself while their families mourned.

Yet, after completing the hardest comeback of his career, both physically and mentally, the emotion could no longer be contained. Joshua broke down during his post-fight interview when crediting his friends for getting him through the first round before quietly saying: 'I don't want to talk about it anymore.'

Anthony Joshua gave an emotional interview after beating Kristian Prenga in Jeddah

When AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary

Joshua was overcome with emotion after the fight, going from a euphoric high to an emotional low within minutes

For months after the crash, Joshua lived with constant pain. Simply getting out of bed became a struggle. He spent two months gently pedalling on a stationary bike before learning how to balance on a stability ball as he rebuilt his body from the ground up.

While the mental toll must have been every bit as demanding, if not more.

That said, Joshua and Eddie Hearn never liked calling this his 'comeback fight'. Seven months out of the ring is hardly unusual for a heavyweight. He had never truly been away from boxing.

But in every way that mattered, this was a comeback.

Because making it back into the ring after losing two of the people closest to him was perhaps Joshua’s greatest challenge of all.

There were moments when returning to the ring did not feel important, or even possible. But eventually, boxing became part of the healing process.

And so, under the bright lights of the Jeddah Superdome and with Latz and Sina embodied on the canvas, Joshua walked back into battle carrying far more than the pressure of victory on his shoulders.

Prenga was never supposed to be the final destination. The Albanian was always viewed as the bridge to something much bigger.

From the moment the fight was announced, it was understood that the real prize was Fury later this year.

This was the tune-up. The opportunity for Joshua to shake off the ring rust, rebuild momentum and remind the heavyweight division exactly who he is.

That is not to say there was no danger. There always is in the heavyweight division and Joshua was reminded of that the hard way.

Prenga entered the contest with 20 knockouts from 20 victories and just a single defeat. The power was genuine. In heavyweight boxing, one punch can change everything, and for a moment it looked as though it might.

The Albanian dominated a chaotic opening round, dropping Joshua twice and threatening to rip up the script.

Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round

But Joshua recovered in the second round, knocking Kristian Prenga out

It's anticipated that Joshua will finally fight Tyson Fury after both heavyweights won their fights this weekend

But there are levels in elite boxing. Prenga had never shared a ring with anyone approaching Joshua's pedigree or experience, and once the former two-time world champion returned to his corner and received a stern dressing down from his coaching team, he emerged with renewed purpose.

Still showing signs of the defensive vulnerabilities that have haunted him throughout his career, Joshua nevertheless displayed the resilience that has defined his comeback. He turned the tide in emphatic fashion, unleashing a devastating combination to stop Prenga 2:43 into the second round.

When Joshua's hand was raised, the emotion he had worked so hard to suppress could finally be contained no longer.

He had warned beforehand that he had kept so much inside. He did not want to centre himself in a story that belonged to grieving families. He wanted to honour his friends privately.

Instead, he pledged lifelong financial support to both families and vowed to continue pursuing the dreams they all shared together.

Yet as victory was confirmed in Jeddah, it was impossible not to think of everything he had endured to get there.

This was never just another win.

But there was one person missing: Tyson Fury.

Only 24 hours earlier, Fury had fought Mariusz Wach in Thailand, going seven rounds before the veteran Pole retired on his stool in a non-televised contest.

All week Fury had insisted he would not be travelling to Saudi Arabia for Joshua's fight and, despite widespread expectation that he would make a late appearance, the former world champion stayed away.

His absence did little to dampen the belief that British boxing's biggest fight is edging closer, but it denied fans the image they have waited years to see.

After so many failed negotiations, collapsed deals and false starts, supporters had hoped to see Joshua and Fury stand face-to-face in the ring for the first time with both men coming off victories.

But experience has taught Joshua not to assume anything in heavyweight boxing.

His long-awaited showdown with Deontay Wilder appeared all but set before Wilder suffered a shock defeat by Joseph Parker in December 2023 on the very same night Joshua won, sending months of planning into the bin.

The heavyweight division has a habit of snatching away the fights everyone wants to see.

Joshua wore a jacket featuring a medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua honoured his friends, Latz and Sina, who were killed in a car crash in December

That is why there will remain a degree of caution until the AJ vs Fury fight is officially confirmed.

Joshua and Eddie Hearn have already revealed that the contract stipulates any showdown with Fury must take place in the United Kingdom because, in their eyes, the biggest fight in British boxing history belongs on British soil.

As things stand, however, Turki Alalshikh and Netflix are understood to favour Madison Square Garden in New York.

That means the contracts will need to be renegotiated.

The expectation is that discussions between all parties will take place over the coming days as they attempt to iron out the remaining details.

For now, Joshua's focus was not on what comes next, but on what he had already overcome.

The tears in Jeddah were not for Tyson Fury.

They were for Latz and Sina.

Sports.title: World Cup hero Vozinha, 40 - who gained 29MILLION followers after denying Lionel Messi - set to join iconic South American club despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami
Sports.content:
World Cup hero Vozinha, 40 - who gained 29MILLION followers after denying Lionel Messi - set to join iconic South American club despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup cult hero Vozinha is set to complete a move to famous Chilean side Colo Colo despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami.

The 40-year-old was one of the heroes of Cape Verde's surprise run to the last-32 stage before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

His standout performances were among the highlights of Cape Verde's debut appearance at the World Cup.

At the start of the Spain match in Cape Verde's World Cup opener, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram, but after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 28.6million followers.

FIFA announced last week that Vozinha had been named in the World Cup's team of the tournament.

Vozinha is expected to join Chilean side Colo Colo despite links to David Beckham's Inter Miami

The keeper was one of the stars of Cape Verde's run to the last-32 stage of the World Cup

Vozinha had been without a club heading into the tournament after leaving Portuguese second division team Chaves at the end of last season.

His availability led to speculation over a possible move to join Messi at Inter Miami, with Vozinha asked about the possibility in a television appearance after the tournament.

'I love football to still be here at 40 years old is because I truly have this passion,' Vozinha said.

'I want to play for at least another one or two years, depending on how my body feels and reacts.

'We never know what tomorrow brings, but I want to keep playing.

'I just hope I can find a club that truly wants me as a footballer, not for marketing purposes.'

Vozinha is now expected to complete a move to Chile's most successful club Colo Colo, who have won a record 34 league titles.

Anibal Mosa, president of Blanco y Negro, the company that manages the Chilean club revealed Vozinha is due to fly to Santiago in the coming days to complete the move.

'Vozinha is going to be a Colo Colo player,' Mosa said.

'In the next few days, he will travel to Chile, undergo the necessary medical examinations, and then be presented here at the Estadio Monumental.'

Colo Colo are currently 12 points clear at the top of Chile's Liga de Primera.

Vozinha has had a nomadic career, playing for clubs in his homeland, Moldova, Slovakia, Cyprus and Portugal's second tier and he has won 94 caps for Cape Verde.

Sports.title: Defensive signings are a MUST after Joe Gomez injury, young star who took his chance and forgotten man Federico Chiesa gives Andoni Iraola food for thought: THINGS WE LEARNED as Liverpool beat Sunderland
Sports.content:
The Andoni Iraola era got off to a flying start in Nashville with a 4-2 thumping of Sunderland – though the injury to defender Joe Gomez may leave the new Liverpool manager pondering at what cost this win came.

Goals from teenager Kieran Morrison, stand-in captain Dominik Szoboszlai, returning loanee Lewis Koumas and Federico Chiesa helped Iraola to a win and pleasing performance over their fellow Premier League opposition.

But the win was somewhat overshadowed by the first-half injury of Gomez and the fact fellow defender Jeremy Jacquet sat the match out due to a fitness concern of his own. It makes the need for a new defender starkly obvious.

Reds expert Lewis Steele was in the city of cowboy hats, hot chicken wings and honky-tonk bars and brings you his key Tennessee takeaways...

Defensive reinforcements are a necessity

It was the sight that no Reds fan, or the transfer committee, wanted to see.

Just seven minutes into the Iraola era, he had his first injury casualty to deal with. Welcome to Liverpool, some may joke, given the well-documented problems with fitness across the board for the team last season.

Joe Gomez went down off the ball, holding what appeared to be a muscular problem. He had a grimace on his face and a look of resignation. The defender missed the majority of 2024-25 and was in and out of fitness last term as his career continues to be plagued by such issues.

The severity of the blow is unclear at this stage and his exit from the pitch may have been merely precautionary – but that does not matter given central defence is a problem area that Iraola noted unprompted in his press conference in Chicago earlier this week.

Joe Gomez was forced off injured just nine minutes into Liverpool's win over Sunderland

Jeremy Jacquet, the new boy signed from Rennes who is hoping to play a significant role this term, is not fit and sat out of this friendly. It is understood Liverpool are going carefully with the young Frenchman after he missed half of last season at Rennes, so want to ease him in slowly.

Jacquet’s last game was February 7 and, even if he was to be as good as everyone at the club hopes and expects him to be, he is still only 21 and needs to settle into the physical demands of English football.

Virgil van Dijk is not on this pre-season tour and has been given an extended break, given he played more minutes than any player in Europe last term. The Dutchman is now 35 and is heading into the final year of his contract.

The only other senior centre back is Giovanni Leoni, the teenage Italian who signed from Parma this time last year but only made one appearance in which he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament and missed the remainder of the season. His recovery is going well but he is still out.

When he is back, his fitness will need to be managed carefully.

It is also worth recalling that Ibrahima Konate, who played 36 of 38 Premier League games last year, left for Real Madrid on a free transfer.

All of these ingredients add up to one conclusion: Liverpool simply must sign a new defender this summer. Failure to do so leaves them incredibly light in that area and it could cost them dearly.

Morrison takes his chance

Defence is not the only area of the pitch where Iraola’s men are light going into the new campaign, which means there will be chances for youngsters to step up.

It has been one of the key themes of pre-season given plenty of senior stars are absent from this trip, including Van Dijk, Alisson, Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and new signing Victor Munoz, who won the World Cup with Spain. Which kids can step up?

Here in Nashville, it was Morrison who did just that. A goal in the first half was the highlight after Harvey Elliott – back after a forgettable year at Aston Villa – threaded a nice pass to Morrison, who cut in off the right flank and curled a shot into the bottom corner with his left foot.

Kieran Morrison scored Liverpool's opener in a 4-2 win against Sunderland

The 19-year-old, who can play across the forward line, had several other moments of quality and could have notched an assist or two if luck was more on his side.

Northern Ireland are trying to tie down the Manchester-born teenager, who has one senior cap for the national team (he needs to play three times to ensure England cannot poach him at a later date) – and this performance showed why.

He joined Liverpool as an Under-14, having spent eight years at Manchester United as a kid. With several gaps in the forward line – not to mention a Mohamed Salah-sized hole on the right – could Morrison step up?

We won’t get carried away based on one pre-season outing but he was the man of the match here in Tennessee and Iraola must have been impressed. Manchester United’s loss, it would appear, is Liverpool’s gain.

Which other kids stood out?

While the lack of defensive depth is a glaring issue and a worry for many, two who might be rubbing their hands are teenage duo Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who both played the majority of this match.

Ndiaye, 18, was signed from Senegalese side Amitie FC in January having caught the eye at the Under-17 World Cup. He is a physical unit, seems calm in possession and is left-footed, which always helps. He has made the first-team bench several times.

Next to him was Austrian youngster Ndukwe, also 18. Signed from Austria Wien in January, Ndukwe officially joined up with his new team this summer. The 6ft 6in defender is another identified by global talent-spotter Matt Newberry in an intriguing recruitment drive.

21-year-old James McConnell impressed in midfield for Liverpool

Both played well and may be needed this season.

Further up the field, James McConnell was impressive in midfield, Calum Scanlon caught the eye on the left flank with several energetic runs and Josh Abe, who only turned 16 earlier this month, had some nice touches.

Lewis Koumas took his goal with composure after a fine move starring also Dominik Szoboszlai, who was wearing the captain’s armband.

Chiesa shows Iraola what he can do

There are several notable shortcomings to Federico Chiesa’s game that have been well documented by fans. But one thing he has that could be desirable to Iraola is versatility.

He can play on the right wing, left or, as he did here, as a No 9. The Italian scored Liverpool’s third with a well-taken finish from a tight angle then he played a lovely round-the-corner ball in the lead-up to Koumas’s goal.

Chiesa has had a weird career at Liverpool. His first season was a write-off, pretty much, due to injury. The next campaign had some bright moments and big goals but, overall, he never earned the trust of Arne Slot.

Many expected he would leave this summer but is he worth keeping around due to his versatility? It is food for thought for Iraola.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola 'ENDS contract talks with PSG': French star, 23, hands Liverpool a huge boost in race for his signature as Premier League clubs circle young attacker
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola 'ENDS contract talks with PSG': French star, 23, hands Liverpool a huge boost in race for his signature as Premier League clubs circle young attacker

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bradley Barcola has reportedly ended talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a new contract.

The Frenchman's future has been the subject of huge uncertainty, with the 23-year-old entering the final two years of his contract and seemingly unhappy with his bit-part role in Luis Enrique's side.

Liverpool and Arsenal have been strongly linked with the winger. Daily Mail Sport understands that the Anfield club currently have the upper hand in their pursuit of Barcola.

And L'Equipe have reported that Barcola has officially ended talks with PSG over signing fresh terms, blowing the race wide open for his signature.

Bradley Barcola has reportedly ended negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain over a new deal

Reports suggest Barcola has prioritised a move to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool

The French outlet adds that it remains unclear whether the European champions will cash in this summer, with much to be determined across the market as the club pursue RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande.

Bayern Munich and Chelsea also hold an interest in the youngster, although he has reportedly already rejected a move to Stamford Bridge.

Liverpool are in the market for a new winger following Mohamed Salah's departure from Anfield in the summer.

Reports on the continent claim that the sporting project under new boss Andoni Iraola appeals to Barcola.

Sports.content:

The modest £1 each-way stake returned a mammoth £52,252.12 jackpot, leaving the bookies in disbelief.
