Sports.title: Gene Tunney Halts Tom Heeney In Final Championship Defense
Sports.content:
A paid crowd of 43,191 attended, with thousands more admitted on complimentary tickets. The gate reached approximately $691,014.50, producing a net of about $521,422 after expenses. Tunney received a remarkable $525,000 purse, while Heeney earned $100,000. Motion picture rights generated another $20,000. Radio rights produced $15,000.

Referee Eddie Forbes officiated. Charles F. Mathison and Tom Flynn served as judges.

Heeney fought exactly as expected, charging forward in an effort to force exchanges at close range. Tunney relied on disciplined footwork. His steady left jab repeatedly disrupted the challenger before sharp counters landed cleanly. Much of the early action featured clinches as Heeney struggled to trap the champion along the ropes.

By the eighth round, Tunney had opened a damaging cut over Heeney’s left eye. The punishment increased in the 10th when a double jab followed by a chopping right hand dropped the challenger near the ropes. Heeney rose immediately. He kept pressing forward despite absorbing heavy punishment.

The finish came at 2:52 of the 11th round. Tunney unloaded another sustained attack, but Heeney refused to fall. Seeing the exhausted challenger taking unanswered punches, Forbes stepped between them and awarded Tunney a technical knockout victory.

The victory became the final chapter of one of boxing’s finest championship careers. Tunney retired as heavyweight champion. Later that year, The Ring magazine selected him as its inaugural Fighter of the Year for 1928. Heeney earned lasting respect for his determination, although the defeat effectively ended his pursuit of the world heavyweight title.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Outworks Errol Spence Jr. Over 12 Rounds
Sports.content:
The opening rounds were competitive. Tszyu stunned Spence with a right hand in the closing seconds of the first round, but Spence answered in the second with effective body work and a hard left that briefly shifted the momentum. The third round also favored Spence, although Tszyu finished strongly with another right hand.

Tszyu regained momentum in the fourth before another close fifth round. He began taking control in the sixth and seventh, landing the cleaner punches while increasing his work rate. Both fighters developed swelling under their left eyes.

Referee Will Soulos warned Spence several times for low blows in the eighth round as blood began flowing from Spence’s nose. Tszyu continued pressing the action over the final four rounds, repeatedly landing right hands while Spence’s output slowed.

Tszyu finished strongly in the twelfth, rocking Spence with another right hand during the closing minute to seal the victory.

Following the decision, Spence applauded Tszyu before announcing his retirement from boxing.

Reda Defeats Fleming

In the co-feature, Ahmad “Bloodshot” Reda earned a unanimous decision over former Olympian Paul “Showtime” Fleming after 10 entertaining rounds.

Reda controlled most of the early action with his speed and activity, although Fleming enjoyed his best success in the fifth after inviting Reda to exchange while standing against the ropes.

A clash of heads opened a cut over Fleming’s left eyebrow in the seventh. Reda continued to outwork the veteran over the closing rounds despite suffering a cut late in the fight.

The judges scored the bout 99-91, 97-93 and 96-94.

Peters Stops Actis

Australian Olympian Callum “50 Cal” Peters remained unbeaten by stopping Ivan “Gringo” Actis in the seventh round.

The opening rounds featured heavy exchanges before Peters gradually took control with sharper punching. A right hand opened a cut over Actis’ left eye in the fourth, and Peters continued to wear him down until referee Will Soulos halted the bout at 55 seconds of Round 7.

Aokuso Knocks Out Tejeda

Former Olympian Paulo “Sweet P” Aokuso captured the vacant IBF Intercontinental light heavyweight title with a dramatic 10th-round knockout of Luis Antonio Tejeda.

Aokuso rocked Tejeda early, but the Dominican battled back and had the Australian badly hurt against the ropes during the seventh round.

The fight ended suddenly in the final round when Aokuso landed a crushing counter left hand that flattened Tejeda for the count.

Rahimi Wins Pro Debut

Former Olympian Tina Rahimi opened her professional career with a unanimous decision over Sacha Ryan Dryden.

Rahimi boxed well throughout the four-round contest, using her speed and combinations to edge most of the rounds before finishing strongly.

The judges scored it 40-36, 40-36 and 39-37.

Grach Defeats Pluto

Heavyweight Brandon “The Bull” Grach earned a unanimous decision over Ike “From Pluto” Pluto in a five-round battle.

Grach hurt Pluto with a right hand in the third round and scored a knockdown in the fourth. Pluto rallied late and landed several solid punches in the fifth, but Grach had already done enough to secure the victory.

The judges scored the fight 49-45, 49-45 and 48-46.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer for the main event.

Sports.title: Errol Spence Jr. Retires After Tim Tszyu Loss
Sports.content:
Errol Spence Jr. brought his boxing career to an end Saturday night after losing a unanimous decision to Tim Tszyu, saying his health, family and financial security made retirement an easy choice. The former unified welterweight champion made the announcement moments after suffering a 12-round defeat at Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia.

“It was a great fight. Congratulations to Tim and Jeff Fenech. It was a good showing by Tim. I answered a lot of questions about myself, and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life,” Spence said before confirming his decision. “Yeah, for sure. I’ve got my faculties intact. My money is good and working for itself, so everything’s good, man. I’ve got a beautiful family and I thank God that I’m able to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family by my side. Everything’s going to go well.”

The judges scored the fight 117-111, 117-111 and 118-110 for Tszyu, who gradually took control after a competitive opening. Spence was returning from a layoff of nearly three years and showed flashes of his former ability, but Tszyu’s pressure and higher punch output proved decisive over the second half of the contest.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Hands Errol Spence Jr. Tough Return Defeat
Sports.content:
“Middleweight is my new division and I feel strong,” said Tszyu. “This was one hell of a show. There were sleepless nights where I was thinking about facing a legend like Spence. I understand why he’s one of the greats.”

The opening rounds were competitive, with Spence finding success behind his jab and left hand while investing in body shots. Tszyu refused to give ground, walking the former unified welterweight champion down and landing hard right hands whenever Spence paused in front of him.

The fight changed as the rounds wore on.

Tszyu began timing Spence with increasing regularity, connecting with right hands to the head and body while forcing the Texan backward. Spence’s timing and punch output declined as the pace caught up with him, a predictable challenge after such a lengthy absence from the ring.

By the championship rounds, Tszyu had taken firm control. Spence continued fighting back and showed the toughness that defined much of his career, but he spent long stretches covering up, holding and trying to slow the Australian’s momentum. Tszyu never allowed him to regain control, continuing to press forward and outwork him until the final bell.

“The advice from corner was to get in there,” said Tszyu. “I’m trying to replicate Kostya Tszyu and my trainer Jeff Fenech. if I can be half as great as them, I’ll go down as a great man.”

The victory gives Tszyu one of the biggest wins of his career and strengthens his position among the leading names at 160 pounds. He entered the bout under pressure after a difficult run over the last two years, but responded with a disciplined performance against one of boxing’s most accomplished former champions.

“I’d love to fight for a world title. I want Erislandy Lara and all the champions,” said Tszyu. “That’s what I’m aiming for. But beating a great like Errol Spence tops any world title for me.”

After the fight, Spence addressed his future while giving Tszyu credit for his performance.

“It was a good fight and congratulation to Tim,” said Spence. “It’s been a great event and everyone has treated me well. It was a good showing by Tim.

For Spence, the defeat raises fresh questions about what comes next. His decision to return after nearly three years away was one of the sport’s biggest stories, yet the layoff appeared to take its toll as the fight progressed. Although he lasted the full 12 rounds, Tszyu’s steady pressure exposed the difficulty of returning against a proven contender without a tune-up first.

“I answered a lot of questions for myself and now it’s time to go home with my family and start a new life. I’ve got my faculties intact and my money is working for itself. I’m thankful to leave this sport with my family by my side.”

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Eyes Boots Ennis After Bloody Title Defense
Sports.content:
His ambition is understandable. Ennis owns the WBA and WBO titles at 154 pounds, making a unification bout one of the biggest opportunities in the division. Eddie Hearn also backed the idea after the fight, pointing toward a possible event in the United States later this year.

The bigger issue is recovery.

Kelly didn’t leave the ring looking like someone ready to begin another training camp. Agyarko landed plenty of hard punches throughout the contest, and Kelly’s injuries weren’t limited to accidental head clashes. He also complained afterward that the referee allowed too much roughhouse work, describing stretches of the contest as feeling like “an MMA fight.”

That criticism comes with some irony. Kelly repeatedly landed rabbit punches during the fight and eventually had a point deducted for hitting behind Agyarko’s head. Both fighters contributed to the physical nature of the contest.

Kelly has made it clear he wants Ennis next. The bigger question is how long it will take for the damage from the Agyarko fight to heal before he can begin preparing for a unification bout.

Callum Peters remained unbeaten with a seventh-round TKO over Ivan Ricardo Actis in their 10-round middleweight contest. After both men traded hard shots early, Peters gradually pulled away by landing the cleaner punches and forcing Actis onto the defensive. Actis refused to go quietly but absorbed sustained punishment, prompting the referee to stop the fight in the seventh round. The victory extended Peters’ knockout streak and handed Actis the first defeat of his professional career.

Paulo Aokuso scored a dramatic 10th-round knockout over Luis Antonio Tejeda to capture the vacant IBF Inter-Continental light heavyweight title. Aokuso started well before Tejeda battled back, hurting the Australian during the middle rounds and forcing him through several difficult moments. After regaining control late, Aokuso ended the fight with a crushing left hand that left Tejeda unconscious in one of the card’s most spectacular finishes. The victory gave Aokuso the biggest win of his career and provided an early Knockout of the Year candidate.

Grach applied steady pressure throughout while Pluto fired back in an entertaining contest that had the Sydney crowd engaged from the opening bell. The judges scored it 49-45, 49-45 and 48-46 in Grach’s favor after five action-packed rounds. Both heavyweights received praise for stepping in at the last minute and delivering one of the card’s most entertaining fights.

The former Australian Olympian controlled the action with sharp combinations, quick footwork and effective defense while consistently landing the cleaner punches. The victory marked an impressive start to Rahimi’s professional career in front of her hometown fans in Sydney.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Claims Keyshawn Davis Has Gone Missing
Sports.content:
Under the WBO order, the winning bid would be split 75 percent to Haney as champion and 25 percent to Davis as the mandatory challenger. The organization has set a minimum bid of $200,000, although the sides remain free to reach their own agreement before the scheduled hearing.

Bill Haney’s latest post appears aimed at increasing the pressure with little time left on the negotiating clock. Rather than discussing specific terms, he questioned Keyshawn Davis’ willingness to complete a deal while portraying the challenger as absent during one of the biggest business opportunities of his career.

No agreement between the camps has been announced, leaving Monday’s purse bid on course unless a deal is reached beforehand, with time still remaining.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Thought Anthony Joshua’s Career Was Over
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua’s dramatic comeback knockout of Kristian Prenga left Eddie Hearn celebrating by the end of the night, but the Matchroom promoter admitted his thoughts were very different after the opening round.

Joshua climbed off the canvas twice before stopping Prenga in the second round at the Jeddah Superdome, surviving a scare that nearly derailed his comeback.



“When he got dropped, I was like, that’s career over,” Hearn said to Charlie Parsons at The Stomping Ground. “I’m kind of thinking to myself, ‘You know what? I’m proud of him for even getting back in the ring.’ If it ends like this, he should be really proud of the fact that he even returned to boxing. He had 24 breaks in his ribs or something. He couldn’t move, was in hospital for weeks and weeks. To even be in the ring was incredible.” Hearn said Joshua’s recovery changed everything. “He held on. He walked onto an uppercut and somehow found a way to recover,” Hearn said. “When he got back to the stool, I felt if he could just find his legs, this guy had thrown a lot of punches in the first round and was going to wear himself out. AJ has incredible knockout power. It doesn’t matter if he’s hurt. He has the ability to take you out with one punch.” Joshua answered those concerns by stopping Prenga in the second round, but Hearn did not ignore the warning signs. He believes the performance should not overshadow the determination Joshua displayed by overcoming the knockdowns and finishing the fight. Share via: Facebook

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026 : St. Hubert’s Seminary SHS completes comeback against Afua Kobi to book national championship place
Ghana News.content:
St. Hubert’s Seminary Senior High School has staged a remarkable comeback to secure the fifth qualification slot from the Ashanti Regional Qualifiers to the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) national championship.

The Santasi-based school found itself trailing Afua Kobi Ampem Girls’ Senior High School in the opening stages of the contest, but a strong response in the subsequent rounds saw St. Hubert’s regain control and pull away from its opponents.

St. Hubert’s maintained its momentum to finish the contest with 56 points, securing its place at the national championship. Afua Kobi Ampem Girls’ SHS placed second with 50 points, while Toase SHS ended the competition with 33 points.

The victory marked a dramatic turnaround for St. Hubert’s, which refused to be unsettled by its slow start and gradually built enough momentum to secure the crucial win.

With qualification secured, St. Hubert’s now joins the growing list of Ashanti Region representatives preparing for the national championship.

For Toase SHS, the NSMQ journey continues as the school joins Ejisu Senior High Technical School in the third qualification contest.

The two schools will compete for another opportunity to secure a place at the 2026 NSMQ national championship, as the Ashanti Regional Qualifiers continue to produce intense battles for the remaining slots.

Ghana News.title: Emotional scenes as family marks One Year Anniversary of Lumba’s passing
Ghana News.content:
The family of legendary Ghanaian highlife musician Daddy Lumba has marked the first anniversary of his death with an emotional gathering at his East Legon residence in Accra.

The private commemoration brought together family members and close associates who gathered to remember the life and enduring legacy of one of Ghana’s most celebrated musical icons.

In attendance were his kinsmen, his sister, Faustina Fosu and widow, Odo Broni who were inconcollable.

For the first time since his passing, the family offered a glimpse of Daddy Lumba’s final resting place; a tomb located within the mausoleum of his East Legon home.

Surrounding his black tomb is the numerous awards, plaques and musical works that defined his nearly four-decade journey in Ghana’s music industry.

Daddy Lumba, born Charles Kwadwo Fosu, passed away on July 26, 2025, at The Bank Hospital in Accra at the age of 60.

He died after a brief illness, though details about the exact nature of his condition were not publicly disclosed.

Widely regarded as one of Ghana’s greatest highlife musicians, Daddy Lumba left behind a rich catalogue spanning close to four decades, with more than 30 albums and countless hit songs.

A year after his passing, tributes continue to pour in for the man whose voice, melodies and storytelling cemented his status as a timeless figure in Ghanaian music history.

Ghana News.title: First-ever Wa Vendors Expo sparks economic boom and empowers female entrepreneurs
Ghana News.content:
The forecourt of the Upper West Regional Coordinating Council (Ministries) has been transformed into a bustling epicentre of commerce and networking as the Upper West Region hosts its maiden Wa Vendors Expo.

The unprecedented two-day trade fair has successfully drawn vendors from across the country to one central location, creating a vibrant marketplace designed to empower local startups, foster crucial wholesale connections, and champion women in business.

Organised by Mary Baalie, CEO of Masung Royal Stores, the event was borne out of a desire to elevate female entrepreneurs and streamline regional trade.

"It's a trade fair that brings businesses together. We are primarily focused on empowering women, especially those in business, and it also helps create valuable business connections," Baalie explained.

She noted that while many locals have the drive to do business, they often struggle to access wholesale suppliers directly. The expo bridges this gap by bringing diverse regional vendors directly to the people of Wa.

For the participating startups, the high foot traffic has been a game-changer. At Stand 2, a massive crowd flocked to Fari's Bag, where quality items such as cloth bags and towels were being sold for as little as GH₵10. The vendor, Kanton Farihana, was visibly overwhelmed by the huge patronage.

"Since morning when I arrived, I've not rested," she shared, adding that she underestimated the turnout and would need to bring extra help next time to manage the rush. "Because they are affordable and they are quality... I will always come, anytime."

The sheer variety of goods on display has kept attendees captivated and their wallets open. Taadu Amanda, representing Fragrance World by Ella, praised the initiative as an excellent platform to introduce the brand to a new audience, assuring buyers that their products can keep them smelling fresh for up to 48 hours.

Similarly, a representative of Naaj Collections, who travelled all the way from Tamale to participate, attracted curious buyers with a playful marketing pitch by advertising clothes for "only 1 Cedi" before revealing the actual, yet highly affordable, prices. Buoyed by the large crowd and the success of similar events previously held in Tamale, the vendor expressed immense optimism about their sales.

"Alhamdulillah, we are just starting, and you can see the crowd. So there's hope," the vendor said. "Insha'Allah, by tomorrow we'll be going home with 50k! We hope so."

As the first event of its kind in the region, the Wa Vendors Expo is already proving to be a resounding success. It has not only provided a vital financial boost for emerging enterprises but has also firmly demonstrated that the Upper West Region has a strong appetite for dynamic, large-scale commercial opportunities.

Ghana News.title: Joshua knocked down twice as dramatic win sets up Fury fight
Ghana News.content:
Anthony Joshua suffered two knockdowns - the first happening after just 20 seconds - before recovering to dramatically stop Kristian Prenga in the second round of his comeback fight in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The British heavyweight was fighting for the first time since surviving the December car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

He was sensationally rocked by a huge uppercut from underdog Prenga in the opening round, and then hit the canvas again later in the round.

At that point he looked on the verge of one of the biggest shock defeats in heavyweight history, with the long-awaited Tyson Fury fight hanging by a thread.

But Joshua produced one of the greatest escapes of his career, and now that fight is on.

He unleashed his right hand in the second round, with the final shot sending Albanian Prenga crashing down and forcing the referee to halt the contest.

"It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it. It has been tough," Joshua, 36, said.

He choked up and stepped away from the microphone, before adding: "It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

There had been speculation fellow Briton Fury might make an appearance despite insisting he would not attend.

But the master of mind games stayed true to his word, with Fury nowhere to be seen barely 24 hours on from his own warm-up win over Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

"I respect everything he has done and everything that he has achieved, but as a fighting person, we're here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat," Joshua said about the prospect of fighting Fury.

Contracts have been signed, but the venue and date for a fight more than a decade in the making are still unknown.

This chaotic night, however, belonged to Joshua in a victory forged through adversity during the most difficult months of his life.

Joshua extended his record to 30 victories and four defeats in one of the most dramatic fights of his career.

Given the circumstances, this was never going to be a straightforward return for Joshua. Few, however, could have predicted the drama that unfolded inside six minutes.

Joshua carried the names of Ghami and Ayodele on his chest and walked to the ring alongside his entire team in a quiet show of unity. The canvas carried their names too, alongside the words 'My Brother's Keeper'.

His comeback could scarcely have begun in any worse fashion. Just 20 seconds in, a right uppercut from Prenga sent Joshua crashing to the canvas and stunned the arena.

Joshua smiled as he climbed to his feet. Prenga, who arrived with 20 knockouts from his 20 victories but little profile even with boxing's hardcore followers, sensed an opportunity.

Promoter Eddie Hearn barked instructions from ringside, while Joshua stablemate Oleksandr Usyk watched on with a look of concern.

A left uppercut later in the round dumped Joshua on the canvas again. He was still unsteady at the start of the second round and appeared to be there for the taking, but Prenga surprisingly began to box off the back foot and let the Watford fighter off the hook.

Joshua capitalised and, using his years of experience - and perhaps the emotion - he drew Prenga on to a jab before uncorking a crushing right hand. More rights followed as Prenga collapsed to the canvas and the referee had seen enough.

This was 35-year-old Prenga's second loss in his career.

It was Joshua's first test against a recognised professional opponent since Daniel Dubois stopped him in September 2024.

His only fight since had come against YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in December, 10 days before the fatal crash that left him injured.

Joshua passed the Prenga test, but not in the manner anyone expected. It was not the destructive, free-flowing champion who once swept opponents aside.

'Tonight wasn't about Tyson Fury'

Joshua made his pro debut in 2013 after winning gold at the London 2012 Olympics

After defeating 46-year-old Wach in Pattaya, the question of whether Fury would show up to watch Joshua became a subplot of fight night.

A Fury lookalike briefly fooled reporters when he stepped out of a taxi, while Fury's manager Spencer Brown insisted the 'Gypsy King' would be "there in spirit".

The fight between two of the most recognisable names in British boxing is understood to have been agreed for November.

Neither man is at the peak of his powers, but while the commercial appeal remains strong, Joshua's struggles are likely to leave Fury a clear favourite.

The bout is expected to stream on Netflix. British fans are hoping for a homecoming event, but it is understood Saudi organisers and broadcasters favour a venue in the United States to cater for American audiences.

"We've signed the contract. Everything is done," Hearn said.

"But tonight wasn't about Tyson Fury. It was about the strength Anthony Joshua has shown just to be here.

"No-one knows what he's been through over the last seven months. When he went down in the first round, I thought he'd come back too soon."

Ghana’s Amadu Mohammed has secured a quarter final ticket in the men’s Bantamweight - 55kg event at the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026: Edinaman SHS storms to nationals with highest opening score in Central region qualifiers
Ghana News.content:
Edinaman Senior High School has qualified for the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) national championship after recording the highest score on the opening day of the Central Regional Qualifiers.

The Edina-based school delivered a commanding performance in Contest Two, amassing 71 points to secure an emphatic victory over Mando SHS, Nyankumase SHS and Eguafo Abrem SHS.

Edinaman controlled the contest from the opening round, steadily increasing its lead with strong performances in the Problem of the Day, True or False and Speed Race segments before sealing victory with a composed display in the riddle round.

At the end of the contest, the scores stood at:

Edinaman SHS – 71 points

– 71 points Mando SHS – 22 points

– 22 points Nyankumase SHS – 21 points

– 21 points Eguafo Abrem SHS – 10 points

The 71-point tally was the highest recorded by any school on the first day of the Central Regional Qualifiers, reinforcing Edinaman's credentials as one of the region's strongest contenders heading into the national championship.

The victory also makes Edinaman the latest school from the Central Region to secure a place at the 2026 nationals, joining Mfantsiman Girls' Senior High School, which booked the region's first qualification slot earlier in the day.

With more contests scheduled in the coming days, schools across the Central Region will continue battling for the remaining qualification places in Ghana's premier science and mathematics competition.

Ghana News.title: ‘It’s not just an inconvenience’: We’ve underestimated the health impacts of heavy periods
Ghana News.content:
Heavy menstrual bleeding is a serious health condition. Only now are we starting to understand what causes it – and how it can be treated.

From the age of 12-13 onwards, Michelle Alston slept off the worst days of her menstrual periods in the school nurse's office, battling severe pain as she bled through period products. "I was taught that this is just normal," she says. "This is just something that you have to learn to cope with."

She felt weak, failing to cope with her periods as well as her peers seemed to. It wasn't until she reached her early 40s that she learned weakness had little to do with it – her periods were unusually heavy. When bleeding during periods is so extensive that it interferes with quality of life, doctors call it heavy menstrual bleeding, and it's a serious medical problem.

Studies of populations from around the world estimate that between 10 and 30% of reproductive-aged women experience heavy menstrual bleeding like Alston's. And due to under-reporting and a general lack of understanding of how much bleeding is too much, studies suggest it may actually occur in half of all reproductive-aged women. Heavy menstrual bleeding can also signify other health problems and have serious consequences when unchecked, such as anaemia.

Yet, only recently have researchers began exploring the resulting harms from heavy menstrual bleeding in depth, pursuing better diagnostics and treatments. A search of PubMed (a database of biomedical research publications) for the term "menstrual blood" yielded just 400 publications in the last decade. Publications for "semen", for instance, number over 15,000.

"Women are probably owed years, if not decades, of research," says Jackie Maybin, a gynaecologist at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland and programme director of The Missed Vital Sign, a research initiative for heavy menstrual bleeding. "And I think the time is now."

How much blood is too much?

For researchers, heavy menstrual bleeding is blood loss of over 80ml per cycle, blood clots exceeding the size of a US quarter, or periods lasting beyond seven days. But for those of us who menstruate, there's no standardised or metric conversion for the practical ways of measuring bleeding: the number of bathroom visits, pads or tampons changed, or bloodstained pairs of underwear.

Some clinicians try to meet patients halfway, asking them to judge their blood loss using charts featuring progressively bloodier pads and tampons. But that too is imprecise, as all period products aren't created equal and often vary widely in absorption.

As a result, determining how much blood is too much during a period isn't straightforward, and often clinicians have to determine heavy menstrual bleeding by whether it interferes with quality of life.

"The patient sometimes doesn't realise that the amount of bleeding they're having is not normal, and that actually, something can be done about it," says Adwoa Christy, a clinical professor in the department of gynaecology, obstetrics, and reproductive sciences at the University of California, San Francisco.

Alston routinely bled through her sheets and clothes, and once, onto an unforgivingly white chair at a mobile phone shop. She just thought she was doing something wrong, and maybe that she needed different period products to contain the flow.

She was told to accept that experiencing painful cramps and embarrassing bloodstains while on your period is normal. In other regions of the world, period taboos and stigma run deeper.

"I think there are a lot of people in my part of the world who may not complain about it, and who, maybe because of normalisation [of pain] and stigma, don't actually come to a doctor," says Hemantha Senanayake, emeritus professor of obstetrics and gynaecology at the University of Colombo in Sri Lanka and head of the Asian Society of Endometriosis and Adenomyosis (both conditions that can cause heavy menstrual bleeding).

And while gynaecologists may know to ask detailed questions to detect heavy menstrual bleeding, clinicians outside the field may overlook the signs. Alston waited nearly 30 years before someone identified her heavy menstrual bleeding, and she's far from alone.

Heavy menstrual bleeding is not just a symptom

While a problem in its own right, heavy menstrual bleeding is primarily a symptom of a larger issue. It arises from a variety of conditions, including polyps, fibroids, cancer, blood disorders, ovulatory issues, and endometrial disorders, such as endometriosis. It is also common – though still something to address – when someone first starts having periods and during the transition to menopause, when the body’s hormonal choreography is in a period of transition.

Treating these conditions can lessen the heavy bleeding, but scientists still don't know how these conditions interfere with the quantity of blood loss, exactly. "There's been a lot of research focusing on the fibroids themselves, but not why they cause the heavy bleeding, for example," says Maybin, who notes that fibroids are noncancerous growths in uterine muscle.

On the other hand, forgoing treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding can create new problems, such as iron deficiency. Iron is an essential mineral for maintaining healthy cells, immune systems, muscles, skin, hair and nails. Brain fog, dizziness, shortness of breath, easy bruising and hair loss can all set in when iron levels begin to flag.

In this way, the harms of heavy menstrual bleeding persist even outside of menstrual periods: studies estimate that over 40% of women with heavy menstrual bleeding also have iron deficiency. Alston found herself in those statistics too: she was always cold and often craved eating ice cubes, a bizarre but telling clue of iron deficiency that's still poorly understood by researchers. If unaddressed, iron deficiency can escalate to anaemia, in which the bone marrow doesn't have enough iron to produce the requisite haemoglobin for red blood cells to carry oxygen throughout the body – a serious condition that can, in extreme cases, requires blood transfusions to correct.

In low and middle-income countries, Senanayake says, where haemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal death, iron deficiency anaemia that isn't resolved before pregnancy can undermine the body's ability to recover from blood loss. It can also harm the brain development of the foetus.

The costs of heavy menstrual bleeding

While there's growing scientific recognition of the medical seriousness of heavy menstrual bleeding, there's less research on what it's like to live with it.

Like Alston, Emily Young, a lecturer in psychology at Sheffield Hallam University in the UK, experienced heavy menstrual bleeding. She has fainted from blood loss more than once, she explains, and always carried a change of clothes as her unpredictable periods could strike at any time. But her doctors assured her that her periods would settle down once she had a baby. Fuelled by the sting of two decades of dismissal from medical professionals, she now researches the experiences of others with heavy periods.

"It's not just an inconvenience. It is having to structure your entire life around your menstrual cycle," says Young.

Adolescents in the UK with heavy menstrual bleeding miss up to nine days of school per year on average.

For a study published in 2025, Young combed through online forum posts from people with heavy menstrual bleeding to bring similar experiences into focus. What she saw ranged from maddening to darkly funny, she says. Several posts described people needing multiple blood transfusions before a doctor recognised the severity of their problem.

Others contained vivid descriptions, such as, "Yeah, if they ever luminol [a chemical used in forensics to highlight blood at crime scenes] my bathroom, I'm going to jail while they excavate my yard for the obviously dozens of murder victims". There were posts about dropping out of school or work, or not having a healthy sex life due to heavy menstrual bleeding. Some posts mentioned mental health issues, and others, Young says, were heartbreaking, describing suicidal thoughts because periods were so severe and life-altering.

For transgender men or non-binary individuals, periods can be distressing enough – heavy menstrual bleeding adds insult to injury. "We see a lot of transgender patients who identify as male, yet have heavy periods, which is in itself an added horrific experience for them," says Julie Jaffray, a paediatric haematologist at the University of California San Diego Rady Children's Hospital.

Ultimately, the cumulative effects of heavy menstrual bleeding on individuals' personal lives can leak into education and work, and ripple through society. Whenever Alston had her period, she would effectively miss school, she says, sleeping in the nurse's office even though her mother insisted she still attend.

In the UK, on average, adolescents with heavy menstrual bleeding miss up to nine days of school per year. In low and middle-income countries, such as Sri Lanka, Senanayake suspects the numbers are higher. Girls in less affluent areas may attend schools that lack facilities to change or dispose of period products.

During adulthood, this translates to missed work days and opportunities. The last time she had a bad period, Alston, a telehealth therapist in New York City, ended up losing a client when she had to cut their session short. "I couldn't hear her anymore, the pain was so bad," Alston says. "I literally told her: 'I can't finish the session'." After she ended the call, she got up from her chair to see a pool of blood beneath her.

"Women with heavy menstrual bleeding can't go to work for 3.6 weeks of the year [on average]. It's costing the economy billions," says Maybin. "If we get this right for women… we really get it right for everyone in society."

Treatment and trials

There's still a lot of work to do to get it right. While there are treatments available for heavy menstrual bleeding, "it's totally not enough," says Erica Marsh, a professor of obstetrics and gynaecology at the University of Michigan Medical School. "We have frighteningly few interventions."

Treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding depends on the underlying condition. If the bleeding isn't too severe, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, like ibuprofen, can ease the flow. There are hormonal treatments too, such as the birth control pill or hormonal intrauterine devices, one of the most effective treatments at reducing blood loss during periods.

Though these methods are fairly accessible, there are deterrents for their uptake, like pain that can accompany the insertion of a intrauterine device. Birth control worked for Alston, but due to the stigma surrounding the pill in her household, she had to wait until she was older – she got a prescription once she left for college.

Hormonal treatments don't work for everyone, and people often discontinue them due to side effects like tender breasts and mood changes, says Maybin. There are non-hormonal medications people can turn to, such as tranexamic acid, that can staunch the flow. "The issue is they are kind of like a band-aid," says Jaffray, and they don't address the underlying cause.

Medications can't always solve the problem. In her mid-thirties, Alston had come off birth control for a time and her periods came back in full force, with intense mood changes too. She finally saw a gynaecologist who performed an ultrasound and found some potential causes. "She's like, 'Scratch birth control. You have seven or eight large fibroids on your uterus, and you might have endometriosis'," a painful condition in which endometrial tissue that lines the uterus starts growing outside the uterus, Alston recalls.

As a result, she chose to have a hysterectomy and completely remove her uterus. In fact, heavy menstrual bleeding is one of the most common reasons people receive hysterectomies. She's happy with her choice, and her heavy menstrual bleeding story ends with a resolution.

But, of course, a hysterectomy is major surgery, it's permanent, and it makes pregnancy impossible. This is especially problematic when providers seem to prioritise fertility over the health of the patient. One of Young's research participants had three children, and her husband had a vasectomy. Her provider still denied her a hysterectomy to treat heavy menstrual bleeding, just in case that the woman got divorced and married another man who wanted children, Young says.

For Maybin, her frustration and embarrassment with the treatment landscape for her patients motivated her to spearhead The Missed Vital Sign, a global research programme funded by the health philanthropy organisation Wellcome Leap. The programme's name reflects the idea that menstrual changes can be the first sign of other health issues, making it a vital sign just like blood pressure, body temperature or heart rate.

Ghana News.title: Sonzele Community Bank works to meet BoG’s GH₵5m capital requirement, declares 25.8% dividend
Ghana News.content:
Sonzele Community Bank PLC has launched an aggressive share mobilisation campaign to meet the Bank of Ghana's (BoG) new GH₵5 million minimum capital requirement by December 2026 while rewarding its shareholders with a substantial 25.8% dividend payout for the 2025 financial year.

The bank, which currently has a stated capital of GH₵2.28 million, is calling on indigenes, members of the diaspora, and the youth to increase their investments to bridge the capital shortfall and secure the financial institution's future.

Speaking at the bank's 36th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Jirapa, Board Chairman Michael Zusain revealed that despite economic turbulence and falling Treasury bill rates, the bank's total assets grew by 19.19% to GH₵84.3 million in 2025.

Outlining the regulator's new directive, Mr Zusain noted that the BoG now requires all rural and community banks to rebrand.

"The Bank of Ghana has recently issued a directive requiring all rural and community banks in the country to change their names to 'Community Banks' and to increase their minimum stated capital from GH₵1 million to GH₵5 million by 31 December 2026," Mr Zusain stated.

To mitigate the economic shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, the central bank had previously halted dividend payments for seven years. However, following a pre-tax profit of GH₵3.7 million in 2025, Sonzele Community Bank secured regulatory approval to reward its investors.

"The Board is proposing a payment of GH₵0.258 per share for the year under review," the Board Chairman announced, representing an impressive 25.8% return on investment.

Reiterating the bank's financial strength, Chief Executive Officer Abdul-Sallam Bamie emphasised that the rebranding from a "rural bank" to a "community bank" is a strategic move aimed at greater inclusivity, particularly to attract younger investors.

"The change to 'Community Bank' is also intended to provide a wider, much more inclusive identity. Because when you say 'rural bank,' it is limiting," Mr Bamie explained. "I don't know where else you can put your money and get about a 25.8% return in just one year, while your share capital in the bank remains intact."

The urgency of the recapitalisation drive drew high-profile political and traditional support at the AGM. Upper West Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing, who revealed that he is also a shareholder, challenged the people of the region to think beyond the current BoG requirements.

"It is my prayer that by next year, we will all buy shares to enable the bank to grow and become even bigger," the Regional Minister urged. "Maybe one day we will convert it from a community bank into a fully fledged commercial bank once our shareholding and capital increase."

This sentiment was echoed by traditional leaders, who reminded the gathering of the bank's deep roots in the region. Speaking on behalf of the Paramount Chief of Jirapa, Konkuo Naa, Naa Angdelle Haara noted that true banking strength lies in the confidence of the people, not just the size of a building.

"Long before many financial institutions discovered the economic potential of our communities, Sonzele Rural Bank had already laid its foundations here," Konkuo Naa remarked. "Let us honour loyalty with loyalty, and let us continue to uphold and strengthen Sonzele Rural Bank PLC as one of our foremost financial partners in development."

However, the consequences of failing to meet the new capital threshold remain severe. The Wa Branch Manager of ARB Apex Bank, Fred Tweneboa, who spoke on behalf of the Acting Managing Director, Curtis William Brantuo, issued a stern reminder to shareholders about the ticking regulatory clock.

"Failure to bridge the gap within the stipulated timeline may expose the bank to operational limitations, heightened supervisory interventions, or the need to consider alternative strategic options provided under the reform framework," Mr Tweneboa warned.

Local government officials underscored the broader socioeconomic and security implications of a strong local banking sector. The District Chief Executive (DCE) for Nadowli-Kaleo, Mary Haruna, who was the guest of honour, linked sound banking practices directly to community safety.

"The responsibility of recapitalising our community banks rests not only on management and directors but also on every shareholder here who believes in the future of the institution," the DCE stated. "Once you are not sleeping with your money, you will not be the target of armed robbers."

The AGM also highlighted a deep sense of solidarity within the Upper West regional banking fraternity. Fredrick Ahah Diegol, CEO of Lawra Area Community Bank PLC, speaking on behalf of sister community banks, praised Sonzele's financial strength and made a passionate appeal to affluent residents to support other struggling banks in the region to prevent their collapse.

"If we allow two to go down, we will be left with only two giants," Mr Diegol urged. "Don't allow the two struggling banks to go down. Come in your numbers and support us so that we too can stand tall, and together we can be stronger."

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
